'Thou art covered in dirt!'

What did the Pilgrim girl say to her new doll?

Why did the Pilgrims need such a big boat?

What did the Pilgrim's buckle say to his hat?

Why did the Pilgrim bring a broom across the ocean?

Why did the Pilgrims' scarecrow get glasses?

Why don't scarecrows play hide-and-seek on Thanksgiving?

Why did the pumpkin roll all the way to Thanksgiving?

Why didn't the Pilgrims ever feel lost in the New World?

Why did the Pilgrims wear so many layers?

What did the Pilgrim's coat say to the cold?

Why did the Pilgrims' fire keep everyone so happy?

What did the Pilgrims say when the fire crackled?

Why did the Pilgrim kids love their wooden toys?

What did the Pilgrims call their log cabin?
A home sweet log.
Why did the Pilgrims' house always feel cozy?

What did the Pilgrim carpenter say after building his house?

Why did the Pilgrims bring seeds from England?
They wanted to plant a little bit of home.
What did the Pilgrims' first garden grow best?
Hope, and a whole lot of corn.
What did the Pilgrim farmer say on a rainy day?
'Thank the Lord for the rain, my garden is thirsty!'
What did the Pilgrims' corn say to the beans?
'Lean on me, I'll hold you up!'
Why did the Pilgrims plant beans next to their corn?
Because they made great climbing buddies.
What did the squash say to the Pilgrims' corn and beans?
'We make a great team, the three of us!'
Why did the Pilgrims' fields look so tidy?
Everyone kept them in row-der.
What did the Pilgrim kid find in the cornfield?
A whole lot of ears that weren't listening.
Why did the Pilgrims' cornfield go to school?
To become a little more a-maize-d.
What did the Pilgrims say to the very first ear of corn?
'You're a real pop-ular guy!'
What did the Pilgrims' corn say on Thanksgiving?
'Thanks for lending me your ears!'
Why did the Pilgrims thank the sun at harvest?

What do you call a Pilgrim who loves to garden?

What did the Pilgrims' cart say at harvest time?
'I'm carrying a lot of blessings!'
What did the Pilgrim's wheelbarrow say?
'I'm always ready to roll with the harvest!'
Why did the Pilgrims' basket go to the harvest?

Why did the Pilgrim farmer wear a big hat at harvest?
He wanted to keep the sun out of his thanks.
What did the Pilgrim farmer say to his tired horse?
'One more row, then we give thanks!'
What did the Pilgrims call the very first fall in Plymouth?
The beginning of something good.
Why did the Pilgrims' crops grow so well?
They were planted with prayers and hard work.
What did the Pilgrims' harvest say to winter?
'We're ready for you now!'
What did the Pilgrims do after the harvest was in?
They gave thanks and took a well-earned rest.
What do Pilgrim kids and leaves have in common?

Why did the Pilgrim boy rake the leaves before Thanksgiving?

Why was the Pilgrims' maple tree so sweet?
It had a sappy heart.
What did the Pilgrims call the leaf that stayed on the tree?
A real hanger-on.
What did the Mayflower captain say about the cold sea air?
'It's a bit nippy, but full speed ahead!'
Why did the Mayflower sailors love the stars?
They always pointed the way.
What did the Mayflower's compass say?
'I'll always point you in the right direction.'
Why did the Mayflower's sails always look happy?
They were full of wind and full of hope.
What did the Pilgrims say when the storm finally stopped?
'Thank goodness, smooth sailing!'
What did the Pilgrim kids name the Mayflower's waves?
Rocky, Rolly and Splashy.
What did the Pilgrims call the ship's bumpy bunks?
Rock-a-bye beds.
What did the Pilgrim say to the very big wave?
'Whoa, thou art a big one!'
Why did the Pilgrim boy wave at the ocean?
He wanted to see if it would wave back.
What did the Pilgrim girl call her pet seagull?
Captain Squawk.
What did the Pilgrims miss most on the long voyage?
Solid ground under their feet!
Why did the Pilgrims cheer when they saw trees?
It meant the long trip was almost over!
What did the Pilgrims call their first day on land?
A shore-ly good day!
What did the Pilgrims call the end of their long trip?
A happy landing.
What did the Pilgrim grandma say on Thanksgiving?
'Count your blessings, and then count them again!'
What did the Pilgrim grandpa say about the voyage?
'Back in my day, we sailed for 66 days, and we liked it!'
Why did the Pilgrim family sing together on Thanksgiving?
Their hearts were too full to keep quiet.
What do you call a thankful Pilgrim?
A grateful-grim.
What did the Pilgrims call their thank-you list?
The longest scroll in Plymouth.
Why was the first Thanksgiving such a happy day?
Everyone came with a thankful heart.
What did the Pilgrims give thanks for first?
Making it safely across the sea.
What did the Pilgrim say to his new friend on Thanksgiving?
'I'm so thankful we're neighbors!'
Why did everyone at the first Thanksgiving get along?
They were all giving and thanking.
Why do we still celebrate Thanksgiving today?
Because being thankful never goes out of style!
What is the most thankful day of the year?
Thanksgiving, of course!
Why does Thanksgiving come in the fall?
Because that's when the harvest is all in.
What did the kid say after his first Thanksgiving?
'Can we do this again tomorrow?'
What did the family say to Grandma on Thanksgiving?
'Thanks for being the best!'
What did Grandpa say on Thanksgiving morning?
'I'm thankful for every one of you rascals!'
Why did the kids make a thankful tree for Thanksgiving?
So their blessings could branch out!
What did the paper leaf say on the Thanksgiving thankful tree?
'I'm thankful for my family!'
Why did the crayons love Thanksgiving?
They got to color all the fall leaves.
What did the Thanksgiving coloring page say to the crayon?
'You make me so colorful!'
Why was the Thanksgiving thank-you note so happy?
It was full of kind words.
What did the Thanksgiving card say when it got opened?
'Surprise, I'm full of thanks!'
Why did the mail carrier smile on Thanksgiving week?

What did the Thanksgiving family photo say?
'Everybody say thanks!'
Why did the camera love Thanksgiving?

What did the Thanksgiving football say to the kids?
'Let's have a ball!'
What did the tree say to the wind on Thanksgiving?
'Leaf me alone, I'm busy giving thanks!'
What did the Thanksgiving sun say to the morning frost?
'Time to melt away, it's a happy day!'
What did the November frost say to the Pilgrims' pumpkins?
'Stay cool!'
What did the Pilgrims call a crisp Thanksgiving morning?
Brrr-illiant!
Why did the cold wind come to Thanksgiving?
It wanted to blow everyone a hug.
What did the snow say to Thanksgiving?
'I'll see you right after this!'
What did the Thanksgiving fireplace say to the family?
'Come sit close, I've got a warm spot for you!'
Why did the cozy socks love Thanksgiving?
They got to spend all day with the family's toes.
What did the rocking chair say on Thanksgiving?
'I'm rocking with thanks!'
Why did Grandma's rocking chair love Thanksgiving?
It got to rock all the grandkids.
What did the Thanksgiving quilt say to Grandma?
'Thanks for piecing me together!'
What did the knitting needles say on Thanksgiving?
'Let's make something cozy together!'
What did the yarn say on Thanksgiving?
'I'm all wrapped up in thanks!'
Why did the flannel shirt love Thanksgiving?
It was the coziest day of the year.

On Thanksgiving afternoon, Grandpa was telling the grandkids all about the Pilgrims and the Mayflower. His granddaughter asked what kind of music the Pilgrims liked to listen to when they finally got to the new land. Grandpa said he knew for sure.
'Plymouth Rock, of course.'

At Thanksgiving dinner, the grandson proudly told everyone he had learned in math class that pie r squared. Grandma set down the gravy boat and shook her head. She pointed at her fresh pumpkin pie and then at the pan of cornbread.
'No, honey. Pie are round. Cornbread are square.'

Mom cooked so much food for Thanksgiving that the family ate leftovers every night for a week. On the sixth night, the youngest boy came to the table and asked, a little nervously, what they were having for supper. Dad picked up a fork and smiled.
'Thanksgiving, chapter six.'

In school, the teacher showed the class a picture of the Pilgrims with big buckles on their tall black hats. A boy raised his hand and asked why the Pilgrims' pants kept falling down in all the old stories. The teacher said she'd never heard that before.
'Because they wore their belt buckles on their hats!'

The teacher asked the class a Thanksgiving riddle: 'If April showers bring May flowers, what do May flowers bring?' Most of the kids said more flowers, or maybe bees. Then a boy who had been reading about the first Thanksgiving raised his hand.
'Pilgrims!'

The Sunday school class was learning about the Pilgrims who sailed across the ocean to find a new home. The teacher asked if anyone knew what you call the age of a Pilgrim. The kids thought about it for a while, and then a girl giggled.
'A Pilgrim-age!'

At Thanksgiving dinner, Grandpa asked his youngest grandson to say grace. The boy folded his hands and thanked God for the family, the food and the farmers. Then he added, 'And please let Grandma's pie be the one with the crumbly top. Amen.' Grandma patted his hand.
'He already answered that one this morning, sugar.'

Grandma set the cranberry sauce on the Thanksgiving table, still shaped just like the can with the little ridges on it. Her grandson stared at it and asked where cranberries grow. Grandma said they grow in bogs out east.
He said, 'Wow, I thought they grew in cans.'

While the family shucked corn for Thanksgiving dinner, Grandpa told a story about a little baby ear of corn that got lost in the big garden. The baby corn looked everywhere for its family. Finally it found its mama corn and asked one question.
'Mama, where's pop corn?'

After Thanksgiving dinner, Grandma's pumpkin pie had one sad slice left, and it looked a little smushed. Her granddaughter asked why the last slice had to go to the dentist. Grandma said she didn't know.
'Because it needed a filling!'

The pumpkin pie sat on the counter all through Thanksgiving dinner while everyone ate. By dessert time it had a crack across the top, and some of the crust had fallen off. Grandpa looked it over and announced the diagnosis.
'Poor thing's feeling a little crummy.'

The whole family went out to the backyard after Thanksgiving dinner for a game of touch football. Uncle Bob sat in a lawn chair with a big bowl of mashed potatoes and cheered. His nephew asked what you call a potato watching a football game.
'A spec-tater!'
Uncle Dan was on his third plate at Thanksgiving dinner. His sister reminded him that he said he was going on a diet this year. Uncle Dan nodded and said he was sticking to it perfectly.
'I'm on a seafood diet. I see food, and I eat it.'

Every Thanksgiving, the grandkids eat at the card table in the kitchen while the grown-ups eat in the dining room. Ten-year-old Ben asked Grandma how old you have to be before you get to sit at the big table. Grandma smiled.
'You graduate when somebody younger shows up to take your seat.'

After Thanksgiving dinner, Grandpa went straight to his recliner and was snoring in about two minutes. His granddaughter tapped him and asked if he was sleeping through the parade. Grandpa didn't even open his eyes.
'I'm not sleeping, sweetheart. I'm processing my blessings.'
At Thanksgiving, everyone went around the table to say what they were thankful for. When it was Lily's turn, she said she was very thankful for her new baby brother. Mom smiled and asked her why.
'Because now you'll have somebody else to tell to eat their peas.'

The teacher asked the class, 'If the Pilgrims were still alive today, what would they be most famous for?' The kids said the Mayflower, the first Thanksgiving and their funny hats. Then a girl in the front row raised her hand.
'Their age!'

Grandpa was carrying a big pumpkin from the field to make pie for Thanksgiving. It slipped right out of his hands and landed with a thud in the dirt. His grandson ran over and asked what you get when you drop a pumpkin.
Grandpa sighed and said, 'Squash.'

At the harvest festival, a little girl asked the farmer what the scarecrow's favorite fruit was. The farmer said he'd never asked him. The little girl looked at the scarecrow's straw arms sticking out of his shirt.
'Straw-berries, of course!'

Grandpa cut a big corn maze in his field for the grandkids to play in after Thanksgiving dinner. An hour later, the grandkids were all back at the house eating pie, and Grandpa was the one still lost in the maze. Grandma asked him what happened.
'I planned it that way. It kept me away from the pie long enough for you to save me a slice.'

Dad asked the kids a Thanksgiving riddle while they set the table. 'What do you call a turkey that's running down the road as fast as it can?' The kids guessed a runaway and a racer. Dad said they were close.
'Fast food!'

Little Josh wanted to start a family band for Thanksgiving, with Mom on piano and Grandpa on harmonica. He said they already had a drummer, too. Mom asked who in the family was going to play the drums.
'The turkey. He brought his own drumsticks.'

At Thanksgiving, Grandpa asked why the turkey crossed the road. The grandkids said, 'To get to the other side!' Grandpa said that was the old answer, but he had heard a brand new one at the feed store that week.
'To prove he wasn't chicken.'

Grandma offered the turkey a slice of pumpkin pie in the story she was telling the grandkids. She said the turkey shook his head and turned the pie down politely. The grandkids asked why anybody would ever turn down Grandma's pie.
'He said, No thank you, ma'am, I'm already stuffed.'

The family's turkey strutted around the farmyard on Thanksgiving morning looking as relaxed and happy as could be. The neighbor boy asked Grandpa why that turkey wasn't hiding in the barn like the others did every November.
'Because this year Grandma's making ham.'

The volunteer firefighters had Thanksgiving dinner together at the station. Right as the captain said, 'Pass the potatoes,' the alarm went off. The crew answered the call and came back an hour later. Somebody asked how they always ate so fast.
'Thanksgiving at the firehouse is a sprint, not a marathon.'
Dad decided to make the dinner rolls this Thanksgiving all by himself. Halfway through the afternoon, the smoke alarm started beeping and everybody looked at him. Dad calmly opened the oven door.
'Good news, everybody. That's my timer. The rolls are done.'

The family hired a limousine to bring Grandma to Thanksgiving dinner. When the driver opened the door, Grandma handed him four pies in boxes and climbed into the back seat. The driver asked where she would like the pies to ride.
'Up front with you, young man. The pies always ride first class.'

A visitor stopped at the diner in a tiny Missouri town on Thanksgiving week and asked the waitress how many people would be at her family's dinner this year. She said about the same as last year, around three hundred. He asked how she could fit that many people.
'Honey, in this town, Thanksgiving for the family means Thanksgiving for the whole town.'
Dad came downstairs on Thanksgiving morning wearing his oldest, stretchiest sweatpants. Mom asked why he wasn't wearing his nice slacks with company coming over. Dad patted the elastic waistband.
'These are my Thanksgiving pants. They come with an expansion plan.'
After the big Thanksgiving meal, Grandpa leaned back and said, 'I'm sure thankful for the dishwasher.' Grandma was standing at the sink with her sleeves rolled up, washing the roasting pan by hand.
She said, 'Why, you're welcome, dear.'

At Thanksgiving dinner, little Owen poured gravy on his potatoes, his stuffing, his green beans and his roll. When he reached for the pie, Mom stopped him. Grandpa laughed and said that boy was raised right.
'In this family, gravy isn't a side. It's a beverage.'

Little Ellie built a big mountain out of her mashed potatoes at Thanksgiving and poured gravy on top so it ran down the sides. Mom told her to please stop playing with her food. Ellie looked up very seriously.
'I'm not playing, Mama. I'm studying volcanoes for science class.'
The day after Thanksgiving, Dad made a giant sandwich with stuffing, cranberry sauce and a slice of ham, all on one roll. His son asked if that counted as lunch or as another Thanksgiving dinner.
'Son, this is Thanksgiving: The Sequel.'
Mom looked through the fridge the day after Thanksgiving. The pie was gone, the potatoes were gone and the ham was nearly gone. She asked the family which dish had the most leftovers this year.
Everyone said it at the same time: 'The salad.'
Grandma baked nine pies for Thanksgiving, even though there were only eight people coming to dinner. Her granddaughter counted them twice and asked why she made an extra one.
'One for each of you, and one for your grandpa's second helping.'
After Thanksgiving dinner, Grandpa sat down to watch the football game and was asleep before the first quarter ended. When he woke up three hours later, he asked the grandkids who won.
His grandson said, 'The couch did, Grandpa. It pinned you for four quarters.'

Grandma had to borrow ten folding chairs from the church for Thanksgiving dinner. All through the meal, the family sat up extra straight and nobody slouched once. Grandma asked why everyone had such good posture this year.
Grandpa said, 'These are church chairs. They make you behave.'

At Thanksgiving, the old farmer was asked to share what he was thankful for. He said he was thankful for rain in the spring and sunshine in the summer. Then he said there was one more blessing that topped the list.
'And a combine that started on the very first try.'
Driving home from Grandma's house on Thanksgiving night, the kids saw a huge, round, orange moon over the fields. Little Ruby asked her dad why the moon looked so big and full tonight.
'Because it ate Thanksgiving dinner too, sweetheart.'
In the school Thanksgiving play, Annie was cast as the pumpkin pie. Her brother teased her that she didn't even have any lines. Annie said she had the most important part of the whole show.
'Everybody waits for me at the very end.'
At the kids' table, Grandma asked each child what they were thankful for. The oldest cousin said she was thankful for the kids' table itself. Grandma asked why she liked it so much.
'It's the only table where you can eat dessert first and nobody's looking.'
Grandma put her famous sweet potatoes on the Thanksgiving table, covered in melted marshmallows and brown sugar. Her grandson asked if they were a vegetable or a dessert. Grandma winked at him.
'Both. That's how I get you to eat a vegetable once a year.'

Grandma's homemade dinner rolls are the fluffiest in the whole county. A cousin who was visiting for Thanksgiving for the first time asked how light they really were. Grandpa answered before Grandma could.
'So light we have to hold them down with butter so they don't float off.'
After Thanksgiving dinner, Grandma asked little Mia which kind of pie she wanted. 'We have apple, pumpkin, pecan and cherry,' Grandma said. Mia looked at all four pies sitting on the counter.
'Yes, please.'
Mom got up at five in the morning to start cooking Thanksgiving dinner. She baked, boiled, mashed and stirred all day long. When the family finished eating, she looked at the clock and laughed.
'Twelve hours to cook, twelve minutes to eat, and twelve days of leftovers.'
The morning after Thanksgiving, Dad was eating a big slice of pumpkin pie for breakfast. Mom raised her eyebrows. Dad held up his fork and explained that it was actually a very healthy choice.
'It's got eggs, milk and a vegetable. It's basically an omelet.'
Grandma asked everyone at the Thanksgiving table to share what they were thankful for. Grandpa went last. He said he was thankful for every single person at the table, and for all the good food.
'And I'll be even more thankful when somebody passes the potatoes.'

Grandma put a big horn of plenty in the middle of the Thanksgiving table, overflowing with gourds and apples. Her grandson asked why it was shaped like a horn. Grandma said that was a very good question.
'So you can toot about all your blessings.'
On Thanksgiving morning, the kids sang 'Over the river and through the woods, to Grandmother's house we go' as Dad typed Grandma's address into the GPS. The GPS thought for a minute.
Then it said, 'No route found over river. Recalculating through the woods.'

Grandpa always called his granddaughter the apple of his eye. On Thanksgiving, she looked at the dessert table and said she wanted to be something different just for today. Grandpa asked what that might be.
'The apple of your pie, Grandpa. And the first slice.'

On the Monday after Thanksgiving, little Noah wrote a thank-you note to his grandma. He thanked her for the wonderful dinner and said he was sorry about the gravy on the tablecloth. Then he added one more line at the bottom.
'P.S. The dog says thank you for the green beans I didn't eat.'
The family dog always sat under the Thanksgiving table right between the twins. Mom asked why the dog looked so happy every single year, wagging his tail the whole meal.
Dad said, 'Because the twins don't like green beans, and he does.'
Little Sam asked Grandpa what the Pilgrims ate at the very first Thanksgiving. Grandpa said they had corn, fish, squash and maybe some berries. Sam asked if they had any pie at all.
'No pie? Grandpa, that's not a Thanksgiving. That's just a Thursday.'

Uncle Joe heaped a mountain of food on his Thanksgiving plate: potatoes, stuffing, ham, rolls and three kinds of casserole. Grandma told him his eyes were bigger than his stomach. Uncle Joe looked at his plate and nodded.
'Then I'd better start eating with my eyes.'

Every Thanksgiving, Grandma lets the grandkids help make the pies. This year, four-year-old Rosie was in charge of the pie crust. When it came out of the oven lumpy and lopsided, Rosie looked worried. Grandma hugged her.
'Honey, that's not lumpy. That's what we call homemade.'
At Thanksgiving, the little cousins asked Grandpa why their family had a big ham instead of the usual bird. Grandpa said he had a very good reason, and it was all about being a good neighbor.
'A ham never runs off into the woods the night before Thanksgiving.'
After Thanksgiving dinner, the whole family went outside to rake the big pile of fall leaves in Grandma's yard. The kids jumped in it as soon as it was done. Grandpa leaned on his rake and smiled.
'Best rake job ever. Now they'll be too tired to beat me to the last slice of pie.'

Thanksgiving week, the teacher asked her class to draw what they were most thankful for. One boy drew his whole family sitting around the dinner table. In the middle of the table he drew a giant pie that took up half the page.
'That's to scale,' he told the teacher. 'That's exactly how big it looks to me.'

Our new kitten had never seen a CHRISTmas tree before. Every night she climbed a little higher, knocking off ornaments as she went. On CHRISTmas Eve morning we came downstairs and found the angel had fallen off and something else had taken its place at the very top.
It was the kitten, curled up and purring. Grandpa said it was the first tree he'd ever seen with a star that could purr.

Mia wrote a CHRISTmas list three pages long. Mom said, “Sweetheart, that's too many things. Pick the one that's most important and we'll start there.” Mia thought about it for a long time, then crossed out every single item except one.
The only word left was “Batteries.” She explained that everything else on her list needed them.

Little Noah was cast as a sheep in the church CHRISTmas play. His only line was a single “Baa,” and he practiced it for weeks until it sounded just right. When his big moment came, he stepped forward, looked out at the crowd, and spotted somebody in the third row.
He waved with both hooves and shouted, “Hi, Grandma!” The sheep next to him had to say the “Baa” for him.

We spent all afternoon building a gingerbread house with the grandkids. We had candy windows, frosting snow and a peppermint walkway. When we came back from supper, the whole thing had caved in, so we called Grandpa, a retired carpenter, to look at it.
He studied it for a minute and said, “Good news. The foundation's solid. Somebody just ate the walls.”

Aunt Linda came to visit for CHRISTmas and pulled into the driveway with four big suitcases. Dad helped carry them in and asked, very politely, how long she was planning to stay with us. Everyone in the living room got quiet waiting for her answer.
Aunt Linda laughed and said, “Just two nights. The other three suitcases are full of your presents.”

Noah asked if he could bake a birthday cake for Jesus on CHRISTmas Eve. Mom thought that was a sweet idea and helped him frost it white with a big blue star in the middle. Then Dad asked him how many candles he wanted to put on top.
Noah said, “Just one big one. If we put that many on there, Grandpa says the fire department will come.”

Grandpa sat down to decorate CHRISTmas cookies with the grandkids. He worked very hard on a reindeer, but when he held it up, everybody at the table said it looked exactly like a dog. Grandpa looked at it a long time, picked up the red frosting, and fixed it.
He gave it a red nose and announced, “Meet Rover, the Red-Nosed Puppy.” It was the first cookie eaten.

Ella found a big box with her name on it hidden in the back of the hall closet two weeks before CHRISTmas. She picked it up and gave it a good hard shake to figure out what was inside. Then she noticed a second tag taped to the bottom.
It said, “Dear Ella, if you're shaking this, it's socks now. Love, Mom.”

On the way to Grandma's for CHRISTmas, our van slid into a snowbank. Dad said not to worry, because he had packed everything we could possibly need in the back. He got out, walked around and proudly opened the hatch.
Inside were forty wrapped presents, two pies, and one tiny ice scraper the size of a credit card.

Every year the youngest grandchild gets to put the star on top of the tree. This year it was little Ruby, so Dad lifted her up high on his shoulders. She reached out carefully and set it on top, but the star was upside down, pointing straight at the floor.
Grandpa said it was perfect. “Now it's pointing right at the presents, so nobody forgets where they are.”

The church CHRISTmas play had a camel made from two kids under one brown blanket. On the big night, the boy in the front and the boy in the back each thought the other one knew which way to walk. As the music started, they both took off.
The camel went down the aisle in two directions at once. Pastor said it was the first camel he'd seen coming and going.

Our family sang carols in the living room all evening on CHRISTmas Eve. Every time we started a new one, the baby woke up and joined in at the top of her lungs. Finally, around nine o'clock, she drifted off to sleep in Mom's arms.
Mom tiptoed out of the nursery, closed the door ever so softly, and whispered, “Now THAT is a silent night.”

Dad waited in line at the post office for almost two hours to mail our CHRISTmas packages to the relatives. The line went out the door and down the sidewalk. When he finally reached the counter, the clerk smiled and asked how fast he'd like them to get there.
Dad said, “By CHRISTmas.” The clerk said, “Wonderful. Would you like them to get there by NEXT CHRISTmas?”

Dad stayed up until two in the morning on CHRISTmas Eve putting together Lily's new bicycle. The box said “some assembly required,” which turned out to mean all of it. By the time he finished, the bike worked perfectly, but he had six screws left over.
He keeps them in a jar on the workbench labeled “Extra parts. Bike still works. Do not ask.”

Uncle Mike gave little Jacob a full drum set for CHRISTmas. Jacob played it from breakfast until bedtime every day of CHRISTmas break. Dad smiled through the whole thing and sent Uncle Mike a very nice thank-you card.
The next CHRISTmas, Uncle Mike's kids each opened a brand-new trumpet. Dad says it was the best gift he ever gave.

Grandpa bought the grandkids a huge, shiny new toy for CHRISTmas. They tore off the paper, tossed the toy to the side, and spent the whole day playing with the giant cardboard box it came in. They turned it into a fort, a race car and finally a spaceship.
Grandpa said next year he'd save money and just wrap an empty box. Then he crawled inside the spaceship with them.

On CHRISTmas morning we came downstairs to a big surprise. Somehow during the night our dog had unwrapped every single present under the tree. There was paper everywhere, and right in the middle of it all, he was sound asleep wearing a big red bow.
Dad looked around and said, “Well, at least he saved us some time. And he didn't open his own until the end.”

Every CHRISTmas, Grandpa tells the story about walking five miles to school, uphill both ways, through the snow. This year, little Kayla finally raised her hand and asked how a road could possibly be uphill in both directions.
Grandpa winked and said, “You had to be there. And one day, you'll tell your grandkids the very same thing.”

Every year Grandma sets out her nativity set on the mantel. This year she noticed something new standing right beside the shepherds: a green plastic dinosaur. She asked little Henry how it got there, and he explained very seriously.
“Everybody came to see baby Jesus,” he said. “The dinosaur wanted to come too. He promised to be gentle with the sheep.”

Mom mailed out a hundred CHRISTmas cards with our family photo on the front. She didn't notice until they were all in the mail that everyone in the picture had blinked at the exact same moment. Then the phone rang. It was Grandma.
Grandma said, “Lovely card, honey. Everyone looks so peaceful this year.”

Little Max sang “Joy to the World” for the whole family on CHRISTmas Eve. He sang it loud, with lots of feeling, and not one note in the right place. When he finished, Grandma clapped the hardest of anybody in the room.
She said, “Make a joyful noise, that's what it says. And nobody makes a more joyful noise than you.”

Mom told everyone to write thank-you notes for their CHRISTmas gifts before they could play outside. Ten-year-old Ava finished hers in record time. Mom picked up the one to Grandma to check it before she sealed the envelope.
It said, “Dear Grandma, thank you for the purple scarf. Mom says I have to say I love it. I actually do. Love, Ava.”

Dad bragged that he finished all his CHRISTmas shopping in just ten minutes this year. Mom didn't believe him. On CHRISTmas morning she opened the box he handed her and found a snow globe and a bag of beef jerky, both with gas station stickers on them.
She laughed so hard she cried. She said, “Twenty-two years, and you still know exactly what I like.”

Little Sophie loves to sing CHRISTmas songs in the car. On the way to church she was belting out “Winter Wonderland,” but she had one line a little bit wrong. She sang, “Later on, we'll perspire, as we dream by the fire.”
Grandpa said, “With the way your mom keeps the heat turned up, honey, you're not wrong.”

For CHRISTmas, little Ava gave Dad a homemade coupon book. It had coupons for free hugs, a backrub, and one free car wash. In July, on a hot dusty day, Dad pulled out the car wash coupon and handed it to her.
Ava read it carefully and said, “Sorry, Dad. It says CHRISTmas coupon. Come back in December.”

After CHRISTmas dinner, Grandpa always falls asleep in his recliner. This year, while he snored, the grandkids snuck in and stuck a big red bow right on top of his head. When he woke up, he saw himself in the mirror across the room.
Grandpa grinned and said, “Well, I always knew I was a gift.”

We had ham for CHRISTmas dinner. Then we had ham sandwiches, ham soup, ham and eggs, and ham casserole. By the following Friday, Mom opened the refrigerator to start supper and noticed the whole family had quietly left the kitchen.
Even the dog went and hid under the porch.
Every CHRISTmas, Tim gives Dad a necktie. This year was the twelfth tie in a row. Dad held it up, thanked him and asked, kindly, why Tim always picked a tie when he could pick anything at all.
Tim said, “Because you never wear out the other ones, so I figured you must really like them.”

Little Owen played the star in the church CHRISTmas play. He stood on a ladder holding a big shiny star, and the wise men were supposed to follow him across the stage. Owen got so excited when the music started that he climbed down the ladder and started walking.
He led all three wise men straight past the manger and right up to the cookie table.

Max got an Advent calendar with a little piece of chocolate behind each door, one for every day until CHRISTmas. On December first, Mom found every door open and every chocolate gone. She asked him what in the world happened.
Max said, “I'm just getting ready for CHRISTmas a little faster than everybody else.”

We found Grandma's handwritten CHRISTmas cookie recipe card. It said to add one cup of something, but there was a big brown ring smudged right over the ingredient. We brought it to Grandma and asked what it was supposed to say.
Grandma squinted and said, “Oh, that's not flour, honey. That's where I set my coffee cup down in 1972.”

Mom bought matching CHRISTmas pajamas for the whole family photo, including the dog. Everybody grumbled about wearing them, and the dog pulled his off three times. Finally Mom gave up and let him be in the picture without them.
In the photo, everyone looks a little miserable except the dog. He was the only one smiling.
Our teacher gave us a homework assignment over CHRISTmas break. We had to write one full page about our favorite gift. Max turned in a page with just one sentence written right in the middle of it.
It said, “My favorite gift was supposed to be no homework.” She gave him an A for honesty.

The day after CHRISTmas, a gingerbread man limped into the doctor's office. He told the doctor his knee had been hurting him ever since the kids played with him on the kitchen table. The doctor looked it over very carefully and nodded.
The doctor said, “I've got just the thing for that. Have you tried icing it?”

Somebody mixed up the name tags on the gifts this CHRISTmas. Grandpa unwrapped a baby doll with curly hair, and seven-year-old Lily unwrapped a brand-new fishing reel. Everyone laughed and waited for them to trade.
Neither one would trade. Lily caught a bass by New Year's, and the doll still sits in Grandpa's recliner.

Mom hid the CHRISTmas presents so well this year that even she couldn't find them. We searched every closet, under every bed and in the attic. On CHRISTmas morning she had to wrap a few cookbooks from the kitchen shelf instead.
In July she finally found them in the dryer. We had CHRISTmas in July, and Dad said it was the best surprise yet.

Dad ran out of wrapping paper late on CHRISTmas Eve, so he wrapped the last ten presents in the Sunday comics. He was a little embarrassed about it and said he'd do better next year. In the morning the kids sat down by the tree.
Nobody opened anything for twenty minutes. They were all too busy reading the wrapping paper.

Little Ellie asked, “How many sleeps until CHRISTmas?” She asked at breakfast, at lunch, at supper and about thirty times in between. Around the fortieth time, Dad put down his newspaper and looked at her over his glasses.
He said, “Sweetie, if you ask me one more time, it's going to be zero sleeps for me.”

Little Rosie really wanted a part in the church CHRISTmas play, but the only part left was the donkey. Mom worried she'd be sad, because the donkey doesn't have any lines at all. Rosie thought about it and nodded happily.
She said, “That's okay. The donkey carried the most important family in the world. And I can't forget any lines.”

Grandpa wore his new CHRISTmas sweater with real blinking lights to dinner. Everyone said he looked like the brightest thing in the house. Halfway through the mashed potatoes, the battery pack ran out and the lights went dark.
Grandpa just scooted his chair closer to the candles and said, “That's all right. I'll glow on my own.”

Our church's CHRISTmas play needed shepherds, so all the boys wore their dads' bathrobes and tied dish towels on their heads. Little Gus came out with a bright yellow towel that had a big cartoon duck on it. His mom looked at him and gasped.
That was her good kitchen towel. Gus whispered, “Don't worry, Mom. Shepherds didn't care what their towels looked like.”

Little Emma played the angel in the church CHRISTmas play. Her big line was, “Fear not! For behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy.” But when the stage lights came on and she saw the shepherds looking up at her, the words flew right out of her head.
She smiled real big and said, “Don't worry, y'all! It's just me, Emma, and I've got GREAT news!”

Grandpa bought a big electric train set and said it was for the grandkids for CHRISTmas. He set it up all around the bottom of the tree. Every time one of the kids reached for the controller, Grandpa said, “Let me just show you one more time how it works.”
Grandma said he bought it for the grandkids the same way he bought her a fishing pole for her birthday.

Mom asked what everyone wanted for CHRISTmas. Our teenager said, “Money.” Little Jesse thought about it and said, “Money too, please.” Mom raised an eyebrow and said that wasn't very exciting to open.
Jesse said, “Then wrap it in a really big box so it's a surprise.”

Our family drives around town every CHRISTmas Eve to look at the lights. One house had so many lights and inflatable decorations, you could see it from the highway two miles away. Dad slowed the car down to a crawl so everybody could look.
Little Ava pressed her face to the window and whispered, “Dad, I think they can see that one from the moon.”

My little brother wanted to help put up the CHRISTmas tree. Mom gave him one job: hang the ornaments from the box marked “Unbreakable.” He worked very carefully for ten minutes and then came running into the kitchen.
He said, “Mom, good news! I tested every one of them, and they really are unbreakable!”

Grandma always makes her famous fudge on CHRISTmas Eve. This year she let the grandkids help stir, and they stirred and stirred until their arms ached. When it set, Grandma cut it into perfect squares and asked them how they liked their very first batch.
Little Leo said, “It's great, Grandma. But I think it tastes even better when I'm not the one stirring it.”

The whole family drove six hours to Grandma's house for CHRISTmas. We pulled into her driveway after dark, tired and stiff from the long ride. Grandma ran out on the porch, hugged everybody and asked if we'd had a good trip.
Dad said, “Yes, ma'am. We only asked “Are we there yet?” three hundred and twelve times. Mom counted.”

Our church choir practiced “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” for weeks before the CHRISTmas Eve service. On the big night, little Lucy in the front row sang every word perfectly. Afterward, she asked Grandpa a very serious question.
She asked, “Grandpa, who's Harold, and why does he only get to sing once a year?”

Every year on CHRISTmas morning, Dad makes his famous cinnamon rolls. This year he set them on the counter to cool while everyone opened presents. When he came back to frost them, the pan was empty, and the dog was lying under the table looking very innocent.
Dad looked at the dog and said, “Well, I guess somebody already opened HIS present.”

My little sister wanted to give Mom a CHRISTmas gift she made herself. She spent a week in her room with glue, glitter and a shoebox. On CHRISTmas morning, Mom opened it and found a sparkly picture frame with a photo of my sister inside.
My sister said, “It's a picture of your favorite person. You're welcome.”

The snow was coming down hard on CHRISTmas Eve, and Dad had to go out and feed the cows. He bundled up in two coats, three pairs of socks, a hat, earmuffs, a scarf and big leather gloves. Then he waddled to the back door.
He couldn't bend his arms to turn the doorknob, so Mom had to open it and wave goodbye.

Dad decided to put the CHRISTmas lights on the roof this year. He climbed the ladder, hung every light along the gutter, and climbed back down very proud of himself. Then he went to plug them in and realized something.
The plug was on the roof. He climbed back up to get it, and the ladder slid off into the bushes. Mom brought him cocoa up there.

The grandkids helped Grandma set the table for CHRISTmas dinner. Little June was in charge of name cards, and she worked very hard writing everyone's name in her best handwriting. When everybody sat down, Grandpa found his seat at the kids' table.
June said, “You always say you want to be young again, Grandpa. So I gave you a head start.”

Dad was in charge of the turkey for CHRISTmas dinner this year. He read the instructions three times, set the oven, and checked it every twenty minutes. When it was finally done, he carried it out to the table, beaming, with the whole family clapping.
Then Mom asked, “Honey, where's the bag of giblets?” Dad's face fell. “There was a bag?”
ev: Why don't eggs tell jokes?
They'd crack each other up.
What do you call a sleeping bull?
A bulldozer.
Why did the math book look sad?
It had too many problems.
What do you call a fish with no eyes?
A fsh.
Why can't a bicycle stand up by itself?
It's two tired.
What do you call a bear with no teeth?
A gummy bear.
What has ears but can't hear?
A cornfield.
Why did the golfer bring two pairs of pants?
In case he got a hole in one.
What do you call a dinosaur that's sleeping?
A dino-snore.
What did the left eye say to the right eye?
Between you and me, something smells.
What do you call a pig that does karate?
A pork chop.
Why was the broom late?
It over-swept.
How do you make a tissue dance?
Put a little boogie in it.
What did the grape do when it got stepped on?
It let out a little whine.
Why do bees have sticky hair?
They use honeycombs.
What did one wall say to the other?
I'll meet you at the corner.
Why did the kid bring a ladder to school?
To go to high school.
What do you call cheese that isn't yours?
Nacho cheese.
Why did Honu cross the playground?
To get to the other slide.
What kind of tree fits in your hand?
A palm tree.
What's brown and sticky?
A stick.
Why are frogs so happy?
They eat whatever bugs them.
What did the zero say to the eight?
Nice belt.
How do you catch a squirrel?
Climb a tree and act like a nut.
What do you call a boomerang that won't come back?
A stick.
What do you call a cow that plays the tuba?
A moo-sician.
What do you get from a pampered cow?
Spoiled milk.
What's a cow's favorite place to visit?
The moo-seum.
What do you call a cow in an earthquake?
A milkshake.
How do you count a herd of cows?
With a cow-culator.
What do cows sing at birthday parties?
Happy birthday to moo!
Where do baby cows eat lunch?
In the calf-eteria.
What do you call a cow that just had a calf?
De-calf-inated.
What do you get when you cross a cow and a duck?
Milk and quackers.
What do you call a cow that cuts the grass?
A lawn moo-er.
What do you call a cow with a twitch?
Beef jerky.
What do you call a grumpy cow?
Moo-dy.
Why did the cow want to be an astronaut?
To visit the Milky Way.
What do you call a cow that tells jokes?
A laughing stock.
What instrument does a cow play?
The cowbell.
Why did the horse chew with its mouth open?
It had bad stable manners.
What do you call the horse that lives next door?
Your neigh-bor.
How do horses say hello?
Hay there!
Why did the horse go to bed early?
It wanted to hit the hay.
What did the horse say when it tripped?
Help! I can't giddy up!
Why did the pony get sent to its room?
It wouldn't stop horsing around.
Why don't pigs tell secrets?
Because they squeal.
What do pigs put on cuts and scrapes?
Oinkment.
Why did the pig become an actor?
Because it was a real ham.
What do you call a pig that knows karate?
A pork chop.
What do you call a pig with three eyes?
A piiig.
What did the pig say on a hot summer day?
I'm bacon out here!
What do you call a pig that plays basketball?
A ball hog.
What's a pig's favorite ballet?
Swine Lake.
What do you call a pig that drives a truck?
A road hog.
What do you call a pig that paints pictures?
Pablo Pig-casso.
What do sheep do on sunny afternoons?
Have a baa-baa-cue.
What's a sheep's favorite sport?
Baa-dminton.
What do you call a sheep covered in chocolate?
A candy baa.
What did the sheep say to its buddy?
Ewe are my best friend!
What do sheep count when they can't fall asleep?
People!
What do you call a goat on a mountain?
A hill billy.
What did the goat say when it was running late?
I've goat to go!
What do chickens grow on?
Eggplants.
Why did the chicken join the band?
It already had drumsticks.
How do baby chicks dance?
Chick to chick.
Which side of a chicken has the most feathers?
The outside.
What do chickens call a school test?
An egg-xam.
What do you call a chicken that tells jokes?
A comedi-hen.
Why did the chicken go to the library?
It wanted a good bawk.
How does a chicken mail a letter?
In a hen-velope.
What do you call a chicken that counts its eggs?
A mathema-chicken.
How do chickens say goodbye?
Peck you later!
What do you call an egg that goes on safari?
An egg-splorer.
What do you call a duck that gets all A's?
A wise quacker.
What do ducks watch on TV?
Duck-umentaries.
What do ducks like with their soup?
Quackers.
Why did the duck cross the road?
It was the chicken's day off.
What do you call a duck that loves fireworks?
A fire-quacker.
How do ducks fix a leaky roof?
With duck tape.
Where do ducks go when they feel sick?
To the duck-tor.
What's a donkey's favorite party game?
Pin the tail on the human.
What kind of key does a donkey use?
A don-key.
What did the sheepdog say when the flock arrived?
I herd you were coming!
Why are sheepdogs so good at their jobs?
They're herd-working.
What do you call a llama's mother?
A mama llama.
What did the llama say when it was invited on a trip?
Alpaca my bag!
What kind of dog loves bath time?
A shampoodle.
What do you call a dog that can tell time?
A watch dog.
What do you call a frozen puppy?
A pupsicle.
What did the dog say when it sat on sandpaper?
Ruff!
Where do dogs park their cars?
In the barking lot.
What kind of dog does a scientist have?
A Lab.
Why do dogs run in circles?
It's hard to run in squares.
What do dogs eat at the movies?
Pup-corn.
What is a dog's favorite instrument?
The trom-bone.
What do you call a dog on a snowy day?
A chili dog.
Why was the dog such a good student?
It was the teacher's pet.
What do you call a dog with the sniffles?
A germ-an shepherd.
What kind of dog can jump higher than a house?
Any dog. Houses can't jump!
Why don't dogs make good dancers?
They have two left feet.
What do you call a dog that solves mysteries?
Sherlock Bones.
What's a dog's favorite city?
New Yorkie.
What's a dog's favorite breakfast?
Pooched eggs.
Where does a dog go when it loses its tail?
To the re-tail store.
What happened when the dog went to the flea circus?
It stole the show.
What toy train does a puppy love most?
A chew-chew train.
What's a dog's favorite pizza topping?
Pupperoni.
What does a dog write before a final copy?
A ruff draft.
Why did the dog chase its tail?
It was trying to make ends meet.
Why did the Dalmatian go to the eye doctor?
It kept seeing spots.
What do dogs and phones have in common?
They both have collar ID.
What kind of dog sniffs out flowers?
A bud hound.
What do you get when you cross a dog and a calculator?
A friend you can count on.
What do you get if you cross a dog and a daisy?
A collie-flower.
What do you call a pug that hugs everyone?
A hug pug.
What kind of truck does a pug drive?
A pug-up truck.
What's a pug's favorite dessert?
Pug-ding.
Where does a pug nap on a cold night?
Snug as a pug in a rug.
What do you call a pug that loves to dance?
A jitter-pug.
What do you call a pile of kittens?
A meow-tain.
What's a cat's favorite color?
Purr-ple.
What do cats eat for breakfast?
Mice Krispies.
Why was the cat sitting on the computer?
To keep an eye on the mouse.
What do you call a cat that loves to bowl?
An alley cat.
What's a cat's favorite dessert?
Chocolate mouse.
What did the cat say when it lost its toy?
You've got to be kitten me!
What do cats like to read?
Cat-alogs.
What do you call a cat that eats lemons?
A sourpuss.
What do cats wear to bed?
Paw-jamas.
How does a cat bake a cake?
From scratch.
What do cats use to make coffee?
A purr-colator.
What's a cat's favorite magazine?
Good Mousekeeping.
What's a cat's favorite TV show?
The evening mews.
Why did the cat join the Red Cross?
It wanted to be a first-aid kit.
What did the cat say after a long day?
I'm feline tired.
How do cats say thank you?
Thank mew very much.
What's a cat's favorite song?
Three Blind Mice.
Why do cats always get their way?
They're very purr-suasive.
What does a cat put in its drink?
Mice cubes.
Why are cats so good at video games?
They have nine lives.
What is a cat's favorite car?
A Cat-illac.
What's a kitten's favorite school subject?
Mew-sic.
How do cats say hi to each other?
Meow's it going?
What did the cat say when it opened a present?
It's purr-fect!
What do you call a cat who works on an ambulance?
A purr-amedic.
What does a cat say when it's surprised?
Me-WOW!
What's a cat's favorite button on the remote?
Paws.
Who keeps law and order among cats?
Claw enforcement.
What does a cat like on a hot day?
A mice-cream cone.
How do rabbits travel?
By hare-plane.
What do you call a rabbit with fleas?
Bugs Bunny.
What do rabbits use to comb their fur?
A hare-brush.
What is a bunny's favorite music?
Hip-hop.
How do you catch a unique rabbit?
Unique up on it.
What do you call a line of rabbits walking backward?
A receding hare line.
What's a rabbit's favorite dance?
The bunny hop.
What do you call a rabbit that tells jokes?
A funny bunny.
Where do rabbits like to eat breakfast?
IHOP.
What do you call a hamster in a top hat?
Abrahamster Lincoln.
Where do hamsters go on vacation?
Hamsterdam.
What do you call a mouse that's twenty feet tall?
Enor-mouse.
What's a mouse's favorite game?
Hide and squeak.
Why are mice afraid to go swimming?
Catfish!
Why does a mouse love cheese so much?
It's grate!
What do you call a parrot that flew away?
A polly-gone.
What is a parrot's favorite game?
Hide and speak.
Why are fish so smart?
Because they live in schools.
How do fish get to school?
On the octo-bus.
What game do fish love to play?
Name that tuna.
How do you talk to a fish?
Drop it a line.
What kind of fish lives in a birdcage?
A perch.
Why don't fish play basketball?
They're afraid of the net.
What vitamin do fish take?
Vitamin sea.
Why are fish so easy to weigh?
They have their own scales.
What do you call a fish wearing a bow tie?
Sofishticated.
What instrument does a fish play?
The bass guitar.
What do you call a fish that fixes pianos?
A piano tuna.
Why are goldfish orange?
The water makes them rusty.
What fish only comes out at night?
A starfish.
What do fish say when they meet up?
Water you up to?
Why did the fish get such good grades?
It was above sea level.
Where do fish sleep at night?
In a river bed.
Why didn't the goldfish finish its homework?
It was busy swimming in circles.
What do you call a fish with two knees?
A two-knee fish.
What do you call a fish that's a doctor?
A sturgeon.
Which fish costs the most?
A goldfish.

What did the mailbox say to the letter?
Come on in, you're expected.
When is a door not a door?
When it's ajar.
What has a neck but no head?
A bottle.
What has keys but can't open locks?
A piano.
What has teeth but can't bite?
A comb.
What has one eye but can't see?
A needle.
What can fill a room but takes up no space?
Light.
What did the window say to the sun?
Come on in and stay awhile.
Why did the chair go to the doctor?
It had a bad back.
What did the doorbell say to the visitor?
Ding dong, glad you came!
What has a bed but never sleeps?
A river.
What can you hold without touching it?
Your breath.
What has rings but no fingers?
A tree.
What has a thumb and four fingers but isn't alive?
A glove.
What did the spoon say to the bowl?
Let's stir up some fun!
Why was the teapot so relaxed?
It let off a little steam.
What did the plate say to the fork?
Dinner's on me tonight!
Why did the toaster get a gold star?
It always popped up on time.
What did the porch light say to the moth?
Come on over, I'm glowing!
Why did the broom win the contest?
It swept the competition.
What did the vacuum say to the crumbs?
Come on in, there's room for everyone!
Why is the dishwasher always cheerful?
It always comes out clean.
What's a mop's favorite dance?
The swish and swirl.
Where do missing socks go?
On a sock-cation!
Why did the dust bunny hide under the bed?
It was afraid of the vacuum.
What did the trash can say to the kid?
Thanks for taking me out tonight!
Why was the sponge so full?
It soaked up the whole day.
What did the bucket say when it felt sick?
I'm feeling a little pail.
Why did the window washer get a medal?
For seeing things so clearly.
Why was the iron so calm?
It knew how to smooth things over.
Why did the clothespin smile?
It was hanging out with friends.
Why did the dryer get dizzy?
It went around in circles all day.
Why did the laundry go to school?
To learn how to fold.
Why did the dirty dishes call a family meeting?
They wanted to clear the table.
What did the dust cloth say to the table?
I'll leave you spotless!
Why did the lawn mower get a ribbon?
It made the cut.
Why does the rake get invited everywhere?
It always gathers a crowd.
Why did the soap feel so proud?
It was squeaky clean.
What kind of dog loves bubble baths?
A shampoodle.
Why do kids love chore charts?
Checking boxes feels like winning a game.
Why did the button go to the doctor?
It felt a little loose.
What did the zipper say to the button?
You're always so attached!
Why was the sweater so cozy?
It was knitted with love.
Why did the tie go to school?
To get a little knot-ledge.
Why did the scarf stay home?
It was all wrapped up in something.
What did one glove say to the other?
We're always hand in hand.
What did one sock say to the other?
Let's stay a pair forever!
What does a raincoat do on sunny days?
It takes the day off in the closet.
Why did the hat win the race?
It was a head of everyone.
Why did the pajamas go to bed early?
They were all worn out.
Why did the jacket go to the party?
It wanted to zip around with friends.
Why did the belt get a medal?
It held everything together.
Why was the umbrella so popular?
It always came through in a storm.
What did the closet say to the coat?
There's always room for you here.
Why are winter hats so friendly?
They give everyone a warm welcome.
What did the pocket say to the coin?
Make yourself at home!
Why did the boots wait by the door?
They were ready for a muddy adventure.
What did the left shoe say to the right shoe?
Let's go places together!
Why did the shoe go to the doctor?
It had a sore sole.
Why were the sneakers so quiet?
They were sneaking around.
What do you call a shoe made from a banana?
A slipper.
Why did the shoelace stay home?
It was all tied up.
How do shoes say hello?
Heel-o there!
What do shoes do when they're tired?
They rest their soles.
Why did the sneaker say sorry?
It stepped on someone's toes.
Why did the boot get a new job?
It wanted to kick off a new career.
Why did the flip-flop love the beach?
It never had to wear socks.
What did the shoe say to the foot?
You're the perfect fit!
Why was the shoe always on time?
It knew how to step it up.
What kind of shoes do mice wear?
Squeakers.
What do you call a cow that plays an instrument?
A moo-sician.
Why did the drum take a nap?
It was beat.
What's a guitar's favorite vegetable?
String beans!
What kind of music do balloons like?
Pop music!
What do you call a noisy music student?
A treble-maker.
Why was the guitar so tense?
It was too strung up.
Why did the tuba go to the doctor?
It was feeling a little low.
What kind of music do mountains like?
Rock music.
What kind of music do bunnies like?
Hip-hop.
What's a cat's favorite instrument?
The purr-cussion.
Why did the music note take a break?
It needed a rest.
What do you get when you drop a piano down a mine?
A flat minor.
Why did the guitar have so many friends?
It knew how to pick them.
Why couldn't the pianist find the right song?
They were looking in the wrong key.
What did the drum say to the drumsticks?
Let's keep the rhythm going!
Why did the harmonica go to school?
To learn how to harmonize.
Why did the clock join the band?
It had perfect timing.
What kind of band doesn't play music?
A rubber band.
What does a violin wear to a party?
A bow tie.
Why was the trumpet always so proud?
It liked to toot its own horn.
What do you call a fish that plays piano?
A piano tuna.
Why did the tambourine smile?
Everyone kept giving it a shake.
Why was the choir so happy?
Everyone was in harmony.
Why was the singer so cool?
She was surrounded by fans.
What's a kettle's favorite song?
Anything it can whistle.
Why did the cricket sing all night?
It wanted to chirp up the neighborhood.
What did the microphone say to the singer?
Let's make a joyful noise together!
Why do birds sing in the morning?
They're tweeting the day hello.
What did the lullaby say to the baby?
Hush now, I've got this.
Why did the frog join the choir?
It could really hit the low notes.
Why did the sheep join the choir?
It had a ba-a-autiful voice.
What did the hummingbird say when it forgot the words?
Just hum along with me!
Why was the shower such a great stage?
The sound bounced off every wall.
Why don't crabs share their snacks?
They're shellfish.
What do you call a snowman in summer?
A puddle.
What did the shell say to the wave?
Thanks for the ride to shore!
Why was the sandcastle so proud?
It was king of the beach.
What do you call a dog at the beach?
A hot dog.
What kind of hair do oceans have?
Wavy.
Where do sea creatures watch movies?
At the dive-in.
What did the sea say to the sand?
Nice to sea you again.
Why did the sun go to school?
To get even brighter.
Why do sea turtles love the beach?
It's their favorite shell-ebration.
Why are oysters so generous?
They share their pearls of wisdom.
What's a whale's favorite game?
Swallow the leader.
How do fish say hello?
With a fin-tastic wave.
Why did the starfish go to school?
To become a bright star.
Why did the boat go to the doctor?
It had a sinking feeling.
Why was the camping trip so exciting?
Everyone was in-tents!
Why don't mountains get cold?
They wear snow caps.
What did the campfire say to the marshmallow?
You're looking toasty!
What's a camper's favorite letter?
T, for tent!
Why did the owl go camping?
To have a hoot of a time.
Why was the flashlight the star of the camping trip?
It was the guiding light.
Why do bears sleep all winter?
They're bear-y tired.
Why did the stars come out at the campsite?
They wanted to shine with friends.
What did the sleeping bag say at bedtime?
Zip it, it's time to sleep!
Why was the tree so smart?
It had lots of branches of knowledge.
How do trees get on the computer?
They log in.
Why did the s'more win the contest?
It was the toast of the campsite.
Why did the lantern get invited on every trip?
It always lit up the place.
Why did the squirrel love camping?
It was nuts about the outdoors.
What's a vegetable's favorite game?
Squash.
What vegetable is the best listener?
Corn, it's all ears.
Why are gardeners great at card games?
They always have a spade.
Why did the sunflower smile?
It was looking on the bright side.
Why was the garden so peaceful?
Everyone was rooting for each other.
What did the seed say when it grew up?
I'm glad I put down roots!
Why are peas good at hide and seek?
They stay tucked in their pod.
What did the hose say to the flowers?
Water you doing today?
Why did the onion make everyone teary?
It told a sad story in layers.
Why are carrots good for your eyes?
Ever seen a rabbit wearing glasses?
What do you call an angry carrot?
A steamed veggie.
What kind of garden does a baker plant?
A flour garden.
Why are bees so good at school?
They always get B's.
What do you call a cow that eats your grass?
A lawn mooer.
Why did the clock get sent to the principal?
For tocking in class.
Why did the kid throw the clock out the window?
To see time fly.
What does a clock do when it's hungry?
It goes back for seconds.
What goes up but never comes down?
Your age.
What can you catch but not throw?
A cold.
Why did the watch take a vacation?
It needed to unwind.
Why are clocks so calm?
They take things one second at a time.
What did the alarm clock say in the morning?
Rise and shine, sleepyhead!
What did the hour hand say to the minute hand?
Got a minute?
What is always coming but never arrives?
Tomorrow.
Which month has 28 days?
All of them!
Why was the hourglass so patient?
It knew its time would come.
What did the stopwatch say at the race?
I'll be counting on you!
What's the best time to go to the dentist?
Tooth-hurty, at 2:30!
What did the sun say to the clock at sunset?
Let's call it a day!
What gets bigger the more you take away?
A hole.
What has to be broken before you can use it?
An egg.
What can travel the world while staying in a corner?
A stamp.
What belongs to you but others use it more?
Your name.
What month do trees like best?
Sep-timber!
What's a fish's least favorite day?
Fry-day.
What letter is a body of water?
C.
What letter is a question?
Y.
What letter can you drink?
T.
What letter is an insect?
B.
What letter is part of your face?
I.
What letters are never in the alphabet?
The ones in the mailbox.
Why is the letter A like a flower?
A B comes after it.
What word gets shorter when you add two letters?
Short.
What starts with E, ends with E, and has one letter in it?
An envelope.
What's at the end of everything?
The letter G.
What word is spelled wrong in every dictionary?
Wrong.
Which letter is the coolest?
Iced T.
What has words but never speaks?
A book.
What did one bookmark say to the other?
I'll save your place!
Why are books never lonely?
They have lots of characters.
What did the eraser say to the pencil?
Don't worry, I've got your mistakes.
Why did the letter O go to the gym?
To stay well-rounded.
What letter is always doubled?
W, it's a double-U!
What word has five letters but sounds like one?
Queue.
Why didn't Noah play cards on the ark?
Because Noah was standing on the deck.
Where did Noah keep his bees?
In the ark-hives.
What kind of lights did Noah have on the ark?
Flood lights.
Why couldn't Noah do much fishing?
He only had two worms.
Which animal on the ark couldn't be trusted at games?
The cheetah.
What did Noah say as the animals came aboard?
Now I've herd everything!
Why did the elephants pack lightly for the ark?
They already had their trunks.
What animal on the ark had the biggest smile?
The happy-potamus.
Why was the giraffe so helpful on the ark?
It saw the rainbow first.
Why did the snail board the ark early?
It knew the trip up the ramp would take a while.
Why did the animals sleep so well on the ark?
They were all two-tired.
Who was the first tennis player in the Bible?
Joseph, he served in Pharaoh's court.
Where is the first baseball game in the Bible?
In the big inning.
Who was the fastest runner in the Bible?
Adam, he was first in the human race.
How did Jonah feel inside the big fish?
A little down in the mouth.
What kind of car did the disciples share?
A Honda, they were all in one Accord.
Who was the shortest person in the Bible?
Knee-high-miah.
How did Noah keep the kangaroos happy?
He let them hop aboard first.
Why did Noah check on the cats each night?
To be sure they were purr-fectly fine.
Why did the rabbits love the ark?
It was a hop-py voyage.
What did the dove bring back to Noah?
Good news on an olive branch.
Why did Noah's ark have such good music?
Everyone came in pairs, so it was all duets.
Why did the ark never need a map?
Noah was following God's directions.
Who was the best money manager in the Bible?
Pharaoh's daughter, she drew a prophet from the bank.
What did the zebras say to Noah?
We'll take the striped cabin, please.
Why was the ark so cozy at night?
Everyone was snuggled up two by two.
What do you call a baby goat who loves jokes?
A kid at heart.
Why do giraffes take so long to say sorry?
It takes a while to swallow their pride.
What do you call a sheep with no legs?
A cloud.
What's a tornado's favorite game?
Twister.
Why did the rainbow go to school?
To get its colors in order.
Why did the cookie cry?
Its mom was a wafer too long.
Why did the egg hide?
It was a little chicken.
What did the pancake say to the syrup?
You make every morning sweeter!
Why did the jelly bean go to school?
It wanted to be a smartie.
What kind of nut has no shell?
A doughnut.
What's the best thing to put into a pie?
Your teeth!
Why was the dinner table so happy?
Everyone came back for seconds.
Why did Mom put the cake in the freezer?
She wanted it cool for the party.
Why did Dad bring a ladder to the store?
He heard prices were going up.
Why did Mom wear sunglasses in the kitchen?
The kids were so bright today.
What does Dad call his nap on the couch?
Just resting his eyes for a minute.
Why is tag the friendliest game?
Everyone gets a turn to be it.
Why is the hide-and-seek champion never found?
Good players are hard to find.
Why did the kite get invited everywhere?
It always lifted everyone's spirits.
Why did the golfer bring an extra pair of pants?
In case they got a hole in one.
Why does the yo-yo always come back?
It just can't stay away from home.
What did the marble say to the other marbles?
Let's not lose each other!
Why do jump ropes make great friends?
They're always up for a skip.
What did one swing say to the other?
Let's go back and forth about it.
Why did the slide go to the doctor?
It was feeling a little down.
Why are tic-tac-toe players so friendly?
They always give hugs and kisses.

Farmer Ellis had worked the same field for forty years, and this fall the county fair judges finally gave his scarecrow a blue ribbon. A newspaper reporter asked the head judge why a scarecrow made of old overalls and a feed sack had beaten every other entry.
The judge said, 'Simple. He's outstanding in his field.'

A man from the city stopped at a farm and watched the farmer glance at a big herd of cows and say, 'Two hundred and twelve.' The city man was amazed and asked how in the world he could count that many cows so fast. The farmer just shrugged like it was nothing.
'Easy,' said the farmer. 'I count all the legs and divide by four.'

Grandpa was out by the barn digging little holes and dropping something shiny into each one. His granddaughter ran over and saw they were pennies. She asked him why on earth he was planting money in the dirt next to the barn.
Grandpa winked and said, 'Times are tight, sweetheart. I'm trying to raise a little cents.'

At the riddle contest in the Grange hall, the farmer asked the kids, 'If a rooster lays an egg right on the peak of the barn roof, which way will it roll?' Half the kids yelled left and the other half yelled right. Then one quiet girl in the back raised her hand.
She said, 'It won't roll at all, sir. Roosters don't lay eggs.' She won the pie.

A little earthquake rattled a dairy farm one night, but nobody was hurt and nothing was broken. The next morning the farmer went out to milk the cows and came running back to the house all excited. His wife asked what in the world had him so worked up.
He said, 'The cows are just fine, but this morning they gave milkshakes!'

A little boy from the city was visiting his uncle's farm for the very first time. He pointed at an animal in the pasture and asked why that cow didn't have any horns. His uncle patiently explained that some cows are born without horns and some breeds just never grow them.
'And that one,' said his uncle, 'doesn't have horns because it's a horse.'

A horse wandered into the old country store one hot afternoon and stood right at the counter. The storekeeper had seen a lot of strange things in thirty years, but never that. He wiped his hands on his apron, leaned over the counter and asked the only question that came to mind.
'So, why the long face?'

Grandpa took his grandson fishing at the farm pond on Saturday morning. After an hour, the boy's mom called and asked how many fish they had caught so far. The boy held the phone up proudly and said they were doing great. Mom asked for the exact number.
'Well,' he said, 'if I catch this one and two more, I'll have three.'

Uncle Ray came home from the lake with a fishing story that got bigger every time he told it. By supper the bass was about as long as his truck. His nephew asked if he had any proof at all, so Uncle Ray pulled a photo out of his shirt pocket.
'That fish was so big,' he said, 'the picture alone weighs six pounds.'

The game warden walked up to a little boy sitting on the end of the dock with his line in the water. He asked to see the boy's fishing license. The boy said he didn't need one, and the warden asked him how he figured that.
'I'm not fishing, sir. I'm just giving this worm some swimming lessons.'

Grandpa and his grandson rented a boat and found the best fishing spot on the whole lake. The boy grabbed a marker and drew a big X on the bottom of the boat so they could find the spot again next week. Grandpa looked at the X and shook his head slowly.
'Son, what if we don't get the same boat next time?'

A girl at the aquarium asked the tour guide why some fish live in salt water instead of fresh water. The guide started explaining about oceans and rivers and minerals. Her little brother tugged on the guide's sleeve because he was sure he already knew the real answer.
'It's because pepper makes them sneeze.'

Grandma and Grandpa had a fishing contest at the lake. Grandpa brought a brand new rod and a tackle box full of fancy lures, while Grandma brought an old cane pole and a can of worms. By noon Grandma had nine fish and Grandpa had zero. He finally asked her what her secret was.
'Simple,' she said. 'I fish where the fish are, and you fish where the stories are.'

A man walked into the country store and asked for five pounds of birdseed. The storekeeper started scooping it into a sack and asked, friendly-like, how many birds he had at home. The man said he didn't have any birds at all.
'Not yet,' the man said. 'I'm planning to grow some this spring.'

A boy walked into the country store and asked the clerk if they had any broken cookies. The clerk looked in the big glass jar on the counter and said, 'Why yes, we have a few.' The boy shook his head and gave the clerk a very serious look.
'Well, you ought to be more careful with them.'

The old country store on the square had a hand-painted sign that said, 'If We Don't Have It, You Don't Need It.' A smart little boy walked in and asked for an elephant, just to test it. The storekeeper didn't even look up from his newspaper.
'Son, if you needed an elephant, you'd already have one.'

Cousin Jake moved from the big city to a tiny Missouri town and called home to tell everybody about it. His mom asked just how small the town really was. Jake said it was friendly and quiet and had one blinking light, but that wasn't even the best part.
'It's so small the Welcome sign and the Come Back Soon sign are on the same post.'

A traveler stopped at the gas station in a little Missouri town and asked about the weather. That morning it had been sunny, then it rained, then it hailed for two minutes, and now it was sunny again. He asked the man at the counter if it was always like this.
'Mister, if you don't like the weather around here, just wait five minutes.'

On the first day of school, the new teacher asked the class to turn in the homework she had assigned. One boy in the back row raised his hand and said, 'Ma'am, I'm from Missouri.' The teacher smiled and said she was too, so what did that have to do with anything?
'Missouri is the Show-Me State,' he said. 'So you show me how to do it, and then I'll do it.'

The teacher asked the class to name the longest word in the English language. The kids shouted out big words they knew from their science and history books. Then a girl in the front row raised her hand and said it was 'smiles.' The teacher asked her to explain.
'There's a whole mile between the first letter and the last one.'

The science teacher wrote H I J K L M N O on the board and asked the class what it stood for. Nobody had any idea. Finally she gave them a hint that it was something they drink every single day. One boy's eyes lit up.
'It's water! H to O!'

Jimmy came into class twenty minutes late, and the teacher asked what had happened. Jimmy said he'd been walking to school like always, but he passed a road sign and did exactly what it told him to do. The teacher asked what the sign said.
'It said, School Ahead, Go Slow.'

The math teacher asked, 'If I have six apples in one hand and seven apples in the other hand, what do I have?' She was hoping somebody would say thirteen. Everybody was busy counting on their fingers. Then Tommy raised his hand.
'Really big hands, Mrs. Baker.'

Sarah walked up to her teacher's desk and asked very sweetly, 'Mrs. Allen, would you ever punish a student for something she didn't do?' The teacher said of course not, that wouldn't be fair at all. Sarah looked very relieved to hear it.
'Good, because I didn't do my homework.'

During grammar class, the teacher asked, 'What is the plural of mouse?' The class answered, 'Mice!' She asked for the plural of goose, and they said, 'Geese!' Then she asked for the plural of baby, and little Emma's hand shot up first.
'Twins!'

The teacher asked the class to use the word 'fascinate' in a sentence. One girl said she found science fascinating. Another said the museum trip was fascinating. Then Billy stood up proudly, still wearing his winter coat.
'My coat has ten buttons, but I can only fasten eight.'

In art class, a boy turned in a blank sheet of paper. The teacher asked what it was supposed to be, and he said it was a picture of a cow eating grass. She asked where the grass was, and he said the cow ate it. So she asked where the cow was.
'Well, there's no grass left. Why would the cow stick around?'

The history teacher was reviewing for the big test on Friday. She asked the class, 'Where was the Declaration of Independence signed?' She was hoping someone would say Philadelphia. One boy in the third row raised his hand with total confidence.
'At the bottom, ma'am.'

The English teacher was working on proper grammar. She asked Johnny to make a sentence that started with the word I. Johnny said, 'I is...' and the teacher stopped him right there and said, 'No, Johnny, you always say I am.' So Johnny started over.
'I am the ninth letter of the alphabet.'

The teacher walked around the classroom and found Tyler sitting on the floor doing his multiplication problems. She asked him why he wasn't sitting at his desk like everyone else. Tyler said he was only following her instructions.
'You told us to do this without using the tables.'

Mr. Hill asked Marcus where his math homework was. Marcus said, a little sheepishly, that he ate it. Mr. Hill asked why in the world anybody would eat their homework. Marcus said he was just doing what he'd been told.
'You said it would be a piece of cake.'

During geography, the teacher asked the class, 'What's the capital of Missouri?' A boy raised his hand and said, 'M.' The class giggled, and the teacher said that wasn't quite what she meant. He insisted he was right and explained.
'Well, Missouri is always spelled with a capital M, isn't it?'

A man found a penguin wandering down Main Street, so he asked a police officer what to do. The officer told him to take it to the zoo. The next day the officer saw the same man walking down the street with the penguin, now wearing a little hat. He asked why it wasn't at the zoo.
'We went to the zoo yesterday. Today we're going to the movies.'

A snail saved up for years and finally bought a shiny red sports car. Before he drove it home, he had a big letter S painted on both doors. The man at the car lot scratched his head and asked why he wanted an S on his car.
'So when I drive by, everybody will say, Look at that S-car go!'

A duck waddled into the drugstore and asked the clerk for some lip balm. The clerk found a tube and rang it up at the register. When he asked how the duck would like to pay, the duck shook his head and pointed at his own face.
'Just put it on my bill.'

A man walked up to the country store and saw the storekeeper on the porch playing checkers with his dog. The man was amazed and said, 'That has to be the smartest dog in the whole state!' The storekeeper didn't seem impressed at all.
'Not so smart. I've beat him three games out of five.'

A kangaroo kept getting out of its pen at the zoo, so the keepers raised the fence to ten feet. The next morning he was out again, so they made it twenty feet, and then fifty feet. A giraffe leaned over and asked the kangaroo how high he thought they would go.
'Maybe a hundred feet,' said the kangaroo, 'unless somebody remembers to lock the gate.'

A little girl visiting her grandpa's farm noticed that every cow had a bell hanging around its neck. She asked Grandpa why the cows wore bells. Grandpa started to explain about finding them in the woods, but she had already come up with her own idea.
'I know! It's because their horns don't work.'

Two cows were standing side by side in a Missouri pasture on a quiet Sunday afternoon. The sun was warm and the grass was green. The first cow turned to the second and said, 'Moo.' The second cow looked at her for a long time and sighed.
'Well, I was just about to say that.'

A boy asked his grandpa, 'Why do elephants paint their toenails red?' Grandpa said he didn't know. The boy said, 'So they can hide in cherry trees.' Grandpa said he had never once seen an elephant in a cherry tree in his whole life.
The boy grinned and said, 'See? It works.'

On a scorching July afternoon, the family dog stretched out in the middle of the sunny driveway. Mom told the kids to bring him into the shade before he got too warm. The little girl went out, came back laughing, and told everyone what the dog had to say.
'He says he's fine, Mama. He's just a hot dog.'

A man went to the doctor and said, 'Doc, I think I might be a bell.' The doctor handed him a bottle of vitamins and told him to take one a day and get plenty of rest. The man asked what he should do if he didn't feel any better in a week.
The doctor said, 'Just give me a ring.'

Dad was hanging a brand new calendar on the kitchen wall, and the kids asked him what he did with the old one. Dad looked very serious and said he felt sorry for it. The kids asked why anybody would feel sorry for a calendar.
'Because its days were numbered.'

Dad sat in his recliner reading a thick book for three hours and wouldn't come to the table for supper. Mom called him twice. Finally his son walked over and asked what the book was about that made it so hard to stop reading.
'It's about anti-gravity, son. I just can't put it down.'

Little Lily held out her sneakers and asked, 'Daddy, can you put my shoes on for me?' Her dad looked at the tiny pink sneakers, then looked down at his own big feet. He took a deep breath like he was thinking really hard about it.
'I can try, sweetheart, but I don't think they're going to fit me.'

Mom told Ben he couldn't go outside until his room was clean and organized. Ten minutes later he came downstairs and said it was all done. Mom went up and the floor was clear, but she couldn't find a single toy anywhere. She asked how he had organized it so fast.
'Alphabetically. Everything is under B, for Bed.'
