The family loaded up the van for an eight-hour drive to see the cousins. Dad buckled in, adjusted the mirrors and checked the map one more time. Before he even put the van in reverse, a little voice from the back seat asked, 'Are we there yet?'
Dad said, 'Not yet, buddy, but at this rate we'll get there sometime next summer.'

Grandpa took the whole family out to the diner after church. When the waitress came back to check on them, she asked Grandpa, 'How did you find your steak, sir?' Grandpa set down his fork and gave her a big friendly smile.
'Easy. I moved a pea, and there it was.'

Uncle Pete went to the hardware store and bought a big, shiny ladder. The cashier asked if he was painting the house or cleaning out the gutters. Uncle Pete said neither one, and that he had much bigger plans than that.
'I'm taking my life to the next level.'

Little Ava found Grandma's cookie jar on the top shelf of the pantry, but it had a label on it that said VEGETABLES. She asked Grandma why she would put a vegetable sign on a jar full of chocolate chip cookies.
Grandma whispered, 'That's the only jar in this house your grandpa never opens.'

Grandma was knitting in her rocking chair while the grandkids played in the living room. Her grandson asked why she wore her reading glasses all day long, even when she wasn't reading anything. Grandma smiled without looking up from her yarn.
'So I can see what you're up to before you even think of it.'

Grandpa told the grandkids that when he was young he walked to school five miles every day, in the snow, uphill both ways. His grandson asked how a road could possibly go uphill both ways. Grandpa thought about it for a second.
'It was a very confusing road, son. That's why I was always late.'
The grandkids gave Grandpa a fancy new GPS for his truck so he'd never get lost again. A month later they asked how he liked it. Grandpa said he had never even turned it on. They asked him why not.
'I've had one riding in the passenger seat for fifty years, and your grandma has never once said recalculating.'

At his birthday party, Grandpa's granddaughter asked how old he was turning this year. Grandpa said he wasn't exactly sure. She looked worried and said, 'Grandpa, you don't know how old you are?' Grandpa looked at the cake covered in candles.
'Sweetheart, I quit counting when the candles started costing more than the cake.'

At the fire station open house, a little boy pointed at the firefighters and asked why they all wore bright red suspenders. The captain knelt down and said that was a very important question. All the kids leaned in close to hear the big secret.
'To keep our pants up, buddy.'

A firefighter visited the second grade to teach fire safety. He asked the class, 'What should you do when you hear the smoke alarm go off at home?' He expected someone to say get outside fast. One boy's hand shot up first.
'Get outside, and then tell Dad supper's ready.'

Every Sunday the firehouse crew made a big pot of chili and invited the neighbors over. A lady from church asked the captain why firefighters always seemed to be such good cooks. The captain stirred the pot and grinned.
'Ma'am, we just know how to handle the heat.'

The fire crew got a call about a cat stuck high in an oak tree. They raised the ladder, climbed up and gently carried the cat down safe and sound. Ten minutes later, as they were rolling up to leave, the cat was right back at the top of the very same tree.
The captain sighed and said, 'I think she just liked the ride.'

Grandpa served thirty years as a volunteer firefighter before he retired. The first Sunday after, the church bells started ringing and Grandpa jumped up from the breakfast table out of pure habit. Grandma asked him where he was going in such a hurry.
'Sorry. Old habit. I almost showed up for church in full turnout gear.'

During the fire station tour, a little girl covered her ears when they tested the siren. She asked the firefighter why the fire truck had to be so loud. He said there were two reasons, and the first was so cars would get out of the way.
'And the second is so the fire knows we're coming and has time to get nervous.'

A kindergartner asked the big firefighter if he was ever scared of anything. The firefighter said he had run into smoky buildings and climbed tall ladders for twenty years. Then he admitted there was one thing that still made him nervous.
'When my grandkids ask me to help with their math homework.'

A neighbor asked the fire captain how his crew stayed in such good shape when they cooked so much good food at the station. The captain said they had a special workout plan that never fails. The neighbor asked what it was.
'Every time we sit down to eat, the alarm goes off.'

A rookie firefighter asked the captain why the station's coffee pot was older than he was. The captain said that pot had been through more calls than anybody on the crew. The rookie asked if they had ever thought about replacing it.
'Son, that pot is the only one here with more seniority than me.'

Dad was a firefighter, and one Saturday the kitchen faucet started dripping. His son asked if he could fix it, since he worked with water every single day. Dad looked at the faucet and shook his head with a grin.
'Son, I put water on things. Keeping it in things is the plumber's department.'

The church choir couldn't reach the high notes in the big Sunday cantata, so the director asked for ideas. The next Sunday a firefighter in the choir showed up early and set something up behind the back row. The director asked what in the world it was.
'It's my ladder. I figured it'd help us reach those high notes.'

A family hired a stretch limousine to take Grandma to her eightieth birthday dinner. The limo was so long that the kids in the back couldn't even see the driver. Grandma leaned forward and asked the driver just how long this car really was.
The driver said, 'Ma'am, when the front pulls into Branson, the back is still in Springfield.'

A little boy saw a stretch limousine for the first time at his cousin's graduation party. He walked all the way around it twice, counting windows. Then he asked the driver why they called it a stretch limo.
The driver whispered, 'Because it does yoga every morning before work.'

The limo pulled up for a birthday party and all the kids ran out to see it. One little girl counted the doors on the side, then counted them again just to be sure. She looked up at the driver very seriously.
'Is this one long car, or a bunch of short cars holding hands?'

A boy riding in a limousine with his family watched the driver go around a tight corner downtown. The limo swung wide and slow, and somehow didn't touch a single curb. The boy asked the driver how he could turn a car that long.
'Real slow, buddy. I start turning the corner yesterday.'

A lady booked a limousine to take her family out to see the fall leaves. As they climbed in, she asked the driver if he could please take the scenic route today. The driver looked back over his shoulder at the long row of seats.
'Ma'am, in a car this long, every route is the scenic route.'
After a wedding, a little boy watched the limo driver park the big car along Main Street. It took up three whole parking spaces and part of a fourth. The boy asked the driver if that was allowed.
'Son, I didn't park it. I homesteaded it.'

A neighbor kid watched the limo driver hosing down the big white stretch limousine in the driveway. He'd been washing and drying for a long time. The kid asked how long it takes to wash a car that long.
'Well, I start at the front bumper on Monday, and I finish the back bumper Wednesday.'

Grandma hired a limousine to take her to choir practice for her birthday, but they were running late. She tapped the glass and said, 'Young man, step on it!' The driver smiled and explained why that might not help.
'Ma'am, it's so long that if I step on it, the front gets there ten minutes before you do.'

A girl riding in a limousine for her birthday found out it had a TV inside. She was so excited and asked the driver where the remote control was. The driver chuckled and pointed toward the very back of the car.
'It's back there somewhere, sweetheart. It's in a different zip code.'

The Sunday school class was talking about baseball season, and the teacher asked where baseball is first mentioned in the Bible. The kids flipped through their Bibles looking for bats and balls. Finally a girl in pigtails shouted the answer.
'In the very beginning! In the big inning!'

The youth leader told the kids that Moses had the very first tablet. The kids laughed and said there were no computer tablets back then. The leader said Moses' tablet was even more impressive than theirs. The kids asked how that could be.
'His tablet came straight down from the cloud.'

The Sunday school teacher asked why Noah didn't do much fishing during all those days on the ark. The kids guessed it was too rainy, or that he was too busy feeding the animals. A quiet boy in the corner raised his hand.
'Because he only had two worms.'

The Sunday school teacher asked a riddle: 'Which man in the Bible had no parents?' The kids said Adam, which was a good answer. The teacher said there was another one, and one girl who had been reading ahead jumped right up.
'Joshua! He was the son of Nun!'

The teacher asked the class how we know Peter must have done pretty well as a fisherman before he followed Jesus. The kids were stumped and looked at each other. Then the banker's son raised his hand with a big grin.
'Because of his net income.'

During Sunday school, little Ella was drawing very carefully with her crayons. The teacher asked what she was drawing, and Ella said, 'A picture of God.' The teacher gently said, 'But sweetheart, nobody knows what God looks like.' Ella kept right on coloring.
'They will in a minute.'

The Sunday school teacher asked the class if anyone knew the name of Noah's wife. The Bible doesn't actually tell us her name, so the teacher didn't expect an answer. But one boy raised his hand like he knew for sure.
'Joan of Ark!'

At the church potluck, little Caleb went all the way to the back of the line. His mom asked why he wasn't up front with his friends. Caleb said the pastor preached that the last shall be first, so he was waiting for the line to turn around.
Grandpa said, 'Son, that's a promise for heaven. Down here, the last get the corner of the casserole.'

Every family brought a dish to the church potluck, and when the ladies lined everything up there were eleven green bean casseroles and one small plate of ham. The pastor walked the length of the long table and smiled.
'Folks, I believe next year we're starting a sign-up sheet.'

At every church potluck, Mrs. Henderson's chocolate pie disappeared in about two minutes. This year a little boy asked her why she didn't just bake two pies. Mrs. Henderson laughed and said she did bake two pies, every single year.
'The deacons just always find the second one first.'

The Sunday school teacher finished the story of Jonah and asked the class what they thought Jonah was thinking about while he was inside the big fish for three days. The kids guessed he was hungry or cold. One little girl had a different idea.
'He was thinking he should have listened the first time.'

Two cows in the pasture were bored one Friday night. The first cow asked if there was anything fun to do in town. The second cow said there was a new show playing and she'd heard it was really good. The first cow asked where they would go to see it.
'To the moo-vies, of course.'

Farmer Brown's grandkids asked why he never told the pigs any of his secrets, even though he talked to them every morning while he fed them. Grandpa said he learned that lesson the hard way years ago.
'Pigs can't keep a secret. Sooner or later, they always squeal.'

A little girl and her grandpa were watching the bees buzz around his garden. She asked him why bees hum all the time instead of singing like birds do. Grandpa said it was one of nature's great mysteries, but she had already figured it out.
'Because they forgot the words.'
A horse went to the veterinarian because her voice sounded scratchy and she could barely neigh. The vet looked in her throat and listened carefully. The farmer asked what was wrong with his horse.
'Nothing serious. She's just a little hoarse.'

A neighbor came over to borrow Farmer Lee's mule for the afternoon. Farmer Lee said, 'Sorry, the mule's not here today.' Just then, the mule let out a big loud bray from inside the barn. The neighbor said, 'Hey, I can hear him in there!'
Farmer Lee said, 'Now who are you going to believe, me or a mule?'

Grandpa bought the fanciest bird feeder in the store because the box said it was squirrel-proof. By lunchtime there were three fat squirrels sitting right in it, eating all the seed. Grandpa called the company to complain.
The man said, 'Sir, it is squirrel-proof. It's proof that you've got squirrels.'

A frog was driving his little car down a country road when it sputtered and broke down. He called his friend for help. When his friend asked what happened to the car, the frog explained that a big tractor came by and helped him out.
'It's all fine now. My car got toad.'

A boy asked his grandpa why the frogs down at the pond always seemed so happy, sitting on their lily pads and singing all night. Grandpa said frogs have it figured out better than most folks. The boy asked what he meant.
'They just eat whatever bugs them.'

The class took a trip to the zoo and stopped to see the big brown bears. The zookeeper said the oldest bear had lost all his teeth but was still healthy and happy. A little boy asked what you call a bear with no teeth.
'A gummy bear!'
A family visiting the museum asked the guard how old the giant dinosaur skeleton was. He said it was seventy million and three years old. The dad asked how he could possibly know it so exactly.
'When I started working here three years ago, they told me it was seventy million.'

A girl watched a spider building a perfect web in the corner of her grandma's porch. It was so neat and even that it looked like a picture. She told Grandma that spider ought to get a job with computers someday.
'He'd be a great web designer.'
The barnyard animals threw a party, but nobody invited the owl. The rooster said it wasn't because they didn't like him. The pig asked why, then, they had left the owl off the list.
'Because every time somebody tells a story, he keeps asking who.'
Dad used to say he didn't like beards and would never grow one. Then he went on a two-week camping trip and came home with a big bushy beard. His daughter asked him what changed his mind.
'Honestly, sweetheart, it just grew on me.'

A daddy tomato, a mama tomato and a baby tomato were walking to the farmers market. The baby tomato kept falling behind, looking at all the pretty flowers. Finally the daddy tomato turned around, a little bit impatient.
'Come on, son, ketchup!'

Mom spent half an hour looking for her car keys and finally found them in her coat pocket. She sighed and said, 'Well, they're always in the last place you look.' Her son looked up from his cereal with a puzzled face.
'Then why don't you just look there first?'

Little Sam asked his dad if they could get a puppy. Dad said, 'We'll see.' Sam asked his mom if they could get a puppy, and she said, 'We'll see.' Sam marched back to his dad and asked what 'we'll see' really meant.
Dad thought for a moment and said, 'We'll see.'

Mom folded twelve pairs of socks and ended up with eleven socks that didn't have a match. She asked the family where all the missing socks go. Everybody shrugged except Grandpa, who said he had it all figured out.
'They run off to live with all the missing plastic container lids.'

Grandma heard a crash and found little Jack had tossed his alarm clock out the open window into the soft grass. She asked him why in the world he would do that. Jack said he'd heard the saying and wanted to see it for himself.
'I wanted to see time fly.'

When Mom went to make Ethan's bed, she found a wooden ruler tucked under his pillow. She asked him if he had lost it there by accident. Ethan said he put it there on purpose for a very scientific reason.
'I wanted to see how long I slept.'

On the first day of school, a little boy showed up at the bus stop carrying a ladder from the garage. The bus driver asked why on earth he was bringing a ladder to school. The boy said his big sister had told him what grade came next.
'I'm going to high school!'

In math class, the teacher was drawing numbers on the board. She drew a zero right next to an eight and asked the class if they could imagine what the zero might say if numbers could talk. A girl giggled and raised her hand.
'Nice belt!'
A banana went to the doctor because it was turning a little brown and feeling tired. The doctor checked it over and asked what seemed to be the problem. The banana sighed a long sigh.
'I just haven't been peeling very well lately.'

Dad told the family he'd read about a brand new restaurant that was going to open on the moon. He said the food was supposed to be wonderful and the view was out of this world. Mom asked if they should save up and go.
Dad said, 'Nah, I hear it has no atmosphere.'

Grandpa asked the grandkids a riddle at the supper table: 'What's orange and sounds just like a parrot?' The kids guessed a goldfish, a pumpkin and a basketball. Grandpa shook his head at every answer. Finally, he told them.
'A carrot!'

A boy had a dentist appointment, and his mom said they couldn't be late. He asked her what time the appointment was, and she said she couldn't remember. The boy said he knew exactly what time it had to be.
'Tooth-hurty, of course!'
After Sunday dinner, Grandpa fell asleep in his recliner with the ballgame on. His grandson quietly picked up the remote and switched to cartoons. Grandpa's eyes stayed shut, but he spoke right up.
'I was watching that. I was just resting my eyes.'

Grandma got a new phone and called the grandkids on video for the very first time. The whole screen showed only the top of her forehead and the ceiling fan. Her granddaughter laughed and said, 'Grandma, we can only see your forehead!'
'That's all right, sweetheart. It's my best side.'

Grandma was teaching her granddaughter how to make biscuits. The recipe card said a handful of flour, a pinch of salt and a splash of buttermilk. The girl asked exactly how big a handful was supposed to be.
'Well, honey, that depends on whose hand it is.'

Grandpa was teaching his grandson to drive the old tractor in the hay field. The boy asked how fast he should go. Grandpa said, 'Slow.' The boy asked how slow, exactly. Grandpa leaned on the fence post and pointed at the cows.
'Slow enough that the cows can pass you.'

A reporter from the paper interviewed Grandpa on his ninety-fifth birthday. She asked him what the secret was to living such a long and happy life. Grandpa thought about it for a long time, rubbing his chin.
'Well, young lady, the main thing is to keep breathing.'

Grandpa's old pickup truck had over four hundred thousand miles on it. His grandson asked him why he didn't trade the old thing in for a new one. Grandpa patted the dashboard like it was an old friend.
'She's not old, son. She's experienced.'
The country store had a sign in the window that said 'Free Coffee Tomorrow.' A boy came in the next day and asked for his free coffee. The storekeeper pointed at the sign in the window.
'Read it again, son. It still says tomorrow.'

Grandma sent Grandpa to the store and said, 'Get a loaf of bread, and if they have eggs, get six.' An hour later Grandpa came home carrying six loaves of bread and no eggs at all. Grandma asked him what in the world happened.
'They had eggs.'

A man ran into the hardware store and asked for a mousetrap, quick, because he had to catch a bus. The clerk looked at him, then looked out the window at the big yellow bus pulling away from the curb.
'Sorry, mister. We don't have one that big.'

Every afternoon, three old friends sat on the bench in front of the country store whittling sticks with their pocketknives. A little boy watched them for an hour and finally asked what they were making.
One of them held up a pile of curls and said, 'Shavings, son. We're real good at shavings.'

In a small town, everybody knows everybody. When Mrs. Carter sneezed on her front porch, the neighbor across the street hollered 'Bless you!' Then the neighbor next door hollered it too. A visitor asked if that happened every time.
'Oh, yes. And the fourth neighbor down always brings over soup.'

The little Missouri town had its annual parade down Main Street. There was one fire truck, two tractors, the school band and a man with a mule. A visitor asked a local why everyone stayed in their lawn chairs after it passed.
'Because the parade is so short, it goes around twice.'

Two cousins argued at the family reunion about whether you say Missouri or Missour-ah. They asked Grandpa to settle it once and for all. Grandpa leaned back in his lawn chair and gave them a very wise answer.
'Depends on which side of the creek you were born on.'

A man from the city called his brother in a small Missouri town and complained he'd been stuck in traffic for two hours. His brother said they'd had a terrible traffic jam in town that very morning too. The city man asked how bad it was.
'Real bad. Two tractors and a combine, and nobody could get around.'
The small-town newspaper came out every Thursday. A visitor picked up a copy at the diner to see what was going on. The front page had a big headline and a photo that took up half the page.
'Earl's Cow Got Out Again.'
The church youth group was playing basketball when somebody asked why fish never join a basketball team. The youth pastor said he didn't know. The kids looked at each other and grinned.
'Because they're scared of the net!'

Grandpa and his grandson sat in the boat at sunrise. Every time the boy started talking, Grandpa whispered, 'Shh.' The boy finally whispered back and asked why they had to be so quiet in the middle of a big lake.
'So the fish don't hear our plan.'
The teacher announced a spelling test and asked if anyone could spell Mississippi. A boy in the front row raised his hand and asked an important question before he started.
'Do you mean the river or the state?'
The English teacher was teaching about pronouns. She pointed to a boy who was staring out the window and said, 'Name two pronouns.' The boy was startled and turned around.
'Who, me?' The teacher said, 'Very good!'
The geography teacher asked the class to say one good thing about the country of Switzerland. Kids said the mountains, the chocolate and the cheese. Then one boy raised his hand.
'Their flag is a big plus.'
The teacher asked little Johnny what two plus two equals. Johnny said, 'Four.' The teacher said, 'Good.' Johnny folded his arms and looked a little offended.
'Good? That's perfect!'

A girl on her first airplane trip spent the whole flight studying for her spelling test. The flight attendant asked why she was doing homework on vacation. The girl said her teacher always told her she should aim for this.
'Higher education!'
During math class, the teacher asked why the number six was so nervous around the number seven. The class was stumped. A girl in the back counted on her fingers and suddenly laughed.
'Because seven eight nine!'
Dad came in from the garage and told the kids he had a great joke about a roof. The kids begged to hear it. Dad shook his head and said he probably shouldn't tell it.
'It'd go right over your heads.'
Mom asked her son why he was still lying on the couch when he was supposed to be cleaning out the garage an hour ago. He stretched his arms, gave a great big yawn and explained the situation.
'I'm not lazy, Mom. I'm just on energy-saving mode.'
A farm boy watched a hen climb up and sit right on top of the old clock in the barn. He asked his grandpa why that silly hen would ever do a thing like that. Grandpa chuckled and tipped his hat.
'She's just trying to be on time, son.'
The nursery rhyme says the cow jumped over the moon. A little girl asked her farmer grandpa why a cow would ever do such a thing. Grandpa rubbed his hands together on that chilly November morning.
'Probably because the farmer had cold hands.'
Grandpa took the grandkids for a walk through his tall cornfield in late summer. When his granddaughter started to whisper a secret to her brother, Grandpa held up his hand and stopped her.
'Not in here, sweetheart. This whole field is full of ears.'
Grandma was peeling potatoes for supper when her grandson asked why potatoes would make good detectives. Grandma said she had no idea. He grinned and held one up.
'Because they always keep their eyes peeled!'
It was shearing day on the farm, and all the sheep were lined up by the barn. One sheep looked nervous, so the farmer's daughter asked where he thought he was going. The sheep shook his woolly head.
'To the baa-baa shop, of course.'

Grandpa liked to tell jokes while he fed the cows, and every joke had something to do with crops. His grandkids would groan and roll their eyes every time. One day they asked him what you call a farmer who tells jokes like that.
'Corny, and proud of it.'

A boy came home from school and asked his mom why she had some gray hairs. Mom said every time he didn't listen, she got another gray hair. The boy thought about that for a minute and looked at Grandma's beautiful white hair.
'Wow, Mom. You must have given Grandma a lot of trouble.'
The English teacher asked the class to explain the difference between a cat and a comma. Everybody was stumped, so she wrote it on the board for them.
'A cat has claws at the end of its paws. A comma is a pause at the end of a clause.'
The math teacher noticed her math book sitting on the corner of her desk looking very gloomy. A student asked why that book always looked so sad. The teacher flipped through the pages.
'Because it has way too many problems.'
Grandpa's cat liked to curl up right on top of his computer. Grandpa asked the cat to please move so he could check the weather. His grandson said he knew why the cat always sat there.
'She's keeping an eye on the mouse.'
A little boy left his bicycle leaning against the porch, and it kept falling over into the flower bed. His dad asked him why that bike couldn't just stand up on its own. The boy shrugged.
'Because it's two tired.'
The Sunday school teacher asked what kind of lights Noah must have had on the ark. The kids thought about candles and lanterns. Then one girl clapped her hands because she knew the answer.
'Floodlights!'
Grandpa spent a whole afternoon telling the grandkids about how cheap things were when he was young. He said a candy bar cost a nickel and a soda cost a dime. His grandson's eyes got big.
'Wow, Grandpa! How did you ever get rich enough to afford all that?'
Dad came home from the store and announced he had bought a book about how to be more patient. His daughter asked if it was any good. Dad sighed and set it on the shelf.
'I don't know yet. I'm waiting for the right time to read it.'

A visitor to the farm asked the farmer why his scarecrow always looked so happy, standing out in the field in all kinds of weather. The farmer said the scarecrow had a pretty good deal. The visitor asked what he meant.
'He gets paid in hay, and he's always got the best view on the farm.'

The kids asked Grandpa what you call a sleeping bull. Grandpa scratched his head and said he'd never thought about it. His grandson said he knew the answer, and he stomped his feet like a bull to show it.
'A bulldozer!'
A boy at the country store asked the owner why he kept a cat sleeping on the counter. The owner said she worked hard every day. The boy asked what kind of job a sleeping cat could possibly have.
'She's in charge of customer service. She makes sure nobody reads the paper without buying it.'
The church held a pancake breakfast, and the youth group was flipping pancakes. One boy flipped his so high it stuck to the ceiling of the fellowship hall. The pastor looked up and smiled.
'Well, son, I've always said aim high.'

The limo driver picked up three generations of the same family for a birthday dinner. Grandpa sat in the very front seat, Grandma sat in the middle, and the grandkids were way in the back. Grandpa called back to ask how everyone was doing.
The kids shouted, 'Fine, Grandpa! The weather back here is nice too!'

Mrs. Miller asked her third-grade class to use the word “fascinate” in a sentence. Sarah said, “The museum was fascinating.” Tommy said, “The airplanes at the air show fascinate me.” Then little Billy raised his hand, looking very sure of himself.
Billy said, “My coat has ten buttons, but I can only fasten eight.”

The math teacher wanted to make fractions fun, so she held up both hands. She said, “If I have five apples in this hand and six apples in this hand, what do I have?” The whole class thought hard about it. Then Jacob raised his hand from the back row.
Jacob said, “Really big hands, Mrs. Davis.”

Little Jimmy walked into class twenty minutes late. His teacher asked him why he couldn't get to school on time like everyone else. Jimmy said he was being careful because of a sign he saw on the way. The teacher asked what the sign said.
Jimmy said, “It said, School Ahead, Go Slow. So I did.”

The teacher was helping the class with grammar. She said, “Remember, always say ‘I am,’ never ‘I is.’ Now, Johnny, give me a sentence that starts with the word I.” Johnny stood up and began, “I is...” and the teacher stopped him right there and reminded him of the rule.
Johnny nodded and said, “Okay. I am the ninth letter of the alphabet.”

The geography teacher pointed at the big map on the wall. She asked, “Can anybody tell me where the English Channel is?” The class was quiet. Finally little Ruby raised her hand, looking a little sorry for the teacher.
Ruby said, “I don't know, Mrs. Hall. We don't get that channel on our TV.”

When Liam got home from his very first day of kindergarten, Mom met him at the door. She gave him a big hug and asked how he liked school. Liam set down his backpack and looked very tired and very disappointed.
He said, “It was okay. But they didn't finish. They want me to come back tomorrow.”

The teacher asked the class a math question. “If you had ten dollars, and you asked your dad for ten more dollars, how much would you have?” Little Ethan thought about it and answered, “Ten dollars.” The teacher sighed and said, “Ethan, you don't know your math.”
Ethan said, “No ma'am. You don't know my dad.”

During history class, the teacher asked if anyone knew where the Declaration of Independence was signed. She had spent all week on the topic and was hoping for a great answer. Little Grace raised her hand, very confident.
Grace said, “At the bottom.”

The teacher asked the class to name two days of the week that start with the letter T. Most of the kids were stumped. They looked at the calendar and counted on their fingers. Finally Ava raised her hand and gave an answer nobody expected.
Ava said, “Today and Tomorrow.”

Dad came home from work, flopped down on the couch, and said, “Whew. I'm hungry.” He'd been making the same joke for years, waiting for someone to say something. This time, his eight-year-old daughter looked up from her homework first.
She said, “Hi, Hungry. I'm Dad.” Dad said it was the proudest day of his life.

Little Mason asked his dad for twenty dollars to buy a new video game. Dad laughed and said, “Son, money doesn't grow on trees, you know.” Mason thought about that for a long minute while Dad went back to reading the paper.
Mason said, “Then why do banks have branches?”

Mom told Danny to clean his room before he could go outside to play. Ten minutes later he came out and said it was all done. Mom went to check and found the floor spotless and the bed made. She was so impressed she almost cried.
Then she lifted the bedspread and found every toy, sock and comic book he owned, plus a sandwich from Tuesday.

Grandpa took his grandson fishing at the pond behind the church. By lunchtime, the boy had caught six fish and Grandpa hadn't caught a single one. The boy asked Grandpa if he was doing something wrong.
Grandpa said, “Nope. I'm not trying to catch them. I'm just teaching them to be more careful.”

Grandpa told the grandkids that when he was a boy, a candy bar cost only a nickel. The kids couldn't believe it. Grandpa leaned back in his chair and added, “And they were twice as big as they are today, too.”
Grandma said from the kitchen, “No, dear. You were just half as big.”

Grandma's biscuit recipe calls for “a pinch of salt.” Little Abby was helping her bake and asked exactly how much a pinch was supposed to be. Grandma held up her hand and showed her. Abby held up her own little hand to compare.
Grandma said, “Well, honey, that depends on whose fingers are doing the pinching.”
The Johnsons' parrot had heard Mom say “Shoes off at the door!” about a thousand times. Now the parrot said it every time the doorbell rang. Last Sunday afternoon, the pastor stopped by for a visit.
Before anyone could explain, the pastor was standing in his socks, holding his shoes and saying, “Yes, ma'am.”

Our dog knows he is not allowed on the new couch. One day Dad came home and found the dog lying on the floor, but the couch cushion was still warm. Dad told the dog he knew exactly where he'd been all afternoon.
The next day Dad came home early and found the dog standing beside the couch, blowing on the cushion.

Mom was working from home when she stepped away to get coffee. While she was gone, the cat walked across her keyboard and accidentally hit Send on a big report she'd been writing all week. Mom came back and nearly fainted.
An hour later her boss emailed back: “Best report you've sent all year. Keep it up.”

A man walked into the doctor's office and said, “Doctor, you've got to help me. I feel just like a deck of cards.” The doctor looked up from his chart. He had a waiting room full of patients that afternoon.
The doctor said, “Have a seat. I'll deal with you later.”
A fellow came into the doctor's office holding his arm. He said, “Doc, I broke my arm in two places.” The doctor looked at the X-ray, shook his head, and gave the man some very important advice.
The doctor said, “Well, stop going to those places.”

A lady rushed into the doctor's office and said, “Doctor, I feel like a pair of curtains!” She paced back and forth, wringing her hands, and asked him what in the world she should do about it. The doctor set down his pen.
He said, “Ma'am, just pull yourself together.”
A boy came into the doctor's office with his mom. He said, “Doctor, I think I've got a strawberry stuck in my ear.” The doctor looked in his ear with a little light and nodded his head slowly.
The doctor said, “Don't worry, son. I've got some cream for that.”

A man went to see the doctor and said, “Doctor, I think I'm a dog.” The doctor said, “Well, have a seat on the couch and tell me about it.” The man said, “I'm not allowed on the couch.” The doctor asked how long he'd felt this way.
The man said, “Ever since I was a puppy.”

A man went to the doctor and said, “Doctor, I'm shrinking! I used to be six feet tall, and now I'm only five-ten!” He was very upset and wanted to be seen right away. The doctor looked at the full waiting room and smiled at him.
The doctor said, “Well, I'm afraid you'll just have to be a little patient.”

A man walked into the doctor's office, raised his arm over his head, and said, “Doc, it hurts when I do this.” He did it again and winced. Then he did it a third time just to show how bad it was. The doctor nodded thoughtfully.
The doctor said, “Then don't do that.”

Grandpa went to the dentist to have a tooth pulled. The dentist picked up his tools and said, “Now, this might hurt a little bit.” Grandpa gripped the arms of the chair and said, “Go ahead, Doc. I'm ready.” A half hour later, he was all done.
On the way out, Grandpa looked at the bill and said, “Doc, you were right. It hurt a little bit.”

A man brought his car into the shop because it made a strange knocking sound. The old mechanic listened carefully, picked up a hammer, and tapped the engine once. The noise stopped. Then he handed the man a bill for one hundred dollars.
The man asked for an itemized bill. It said: “Tapping with hammer, $1. Knowing where to tap, $99.”

A customer brought her old car to the mechanic and said the brakes were not working very well. She asked him to please fix them as soon as possible. The mechanic worked on the car all afternoon and then called her to come pick it up.
He said, “I couldn't fix your brakes, ma'am. So I made your horn louder.”

A mechanic was working on a car when a famous heart surgeon pulled in for an oil change. The mechanic said, “Doc, I open up engines, fix the valves and put them back together, just like you. So why do you get paid so much more?” The surgeon thought about it.
The surgeon said, “Try doing it with the engine running.”

Grandpa is very proud of his old pickup truck. He tells everyone it has 400,000 miles on it and still has all its original parts. Then he lists the parts he has replaced: the engine, the transmission, the tires, both doors and the tailgate.
When we asked what was still original, he patted the dashboard and said, “The glove box. And me.”

A man walked into the hardware store and said, “I need a thingamajig. You know, the little whatchamacallit that goes on the doohickey.” Most clerks would have been confused. But the old man behind the counter had worked there for forty years.
He said, “Aisle seven, right next to the whatchamacallits.”

A fellow walked up to the counter at the hardware store and said he needed some nails for a project. The clerk asked him, “How long do you need them?” The man thought about it for a second and gave a very honest answer.
He said, “Oh, I'd like to keep them a long time. I'm building a deck.”

A lady walked into the hardware store carrying a crayon. She told the clerk she wanted paint for her kitchen in that exact color. The clerk looked at the crayon, then at her, and said it was a very bright shade of purple. She nodded.
She said, “My granddaughter colored the kitchen wall with it. I figured it'd be easier to match her than scrub it off.”

A man came into the hardware store and asked for a can opener. The clerk brought him one, and the man tried it on a can of beans right there at the counter. It didn't work at all. The man handed it back and asked what in the world it was.
The clerk looked at it and said, “Oh, sorry. That's our can't opener.”

Little Sophie made breakfast in bed for Mom on Mother's Day. She brought up a tray with orange juice and a big plate of very, very dark toast. Mom took a bite, smiled and said it was the best toast she'd ever had.
Sophie said, “Good! Because I used the whole loaf practicing.”

Dad was trying to bake a cake from Grandma's recipe card. It said, “Separate two eggs.” Dad scratched his head for a minute, then went to work. When Mom came in an hour later, she couldn't find the eggs anywhere.
One egg was in the kitchen, and the other was all the way upstairs in the bathroom cabinet.

Mom left a note for Dad that said to put the casserole in the oven at 350 degrees for one hour. When she got home, she found Dad still sitting in front of the oven, watching it. She asked why he was just sitting there.
Dad said, “Our oven only goes to 350 once. I set it at 175 and doubled the time.”

The cookbook said Grandma's lasagna recipe would serve four people. We made one pan for the family on Sunday after church. Dad got his plate first, and by the time the rest of us sat down, the pan was nearly empty.
Mom read the recipe card again and wrote at the bottom: “Serves four, unless one of them is Dad.”
Little Leo was helping Grandma bake cookies. Grandma said, “Now add a dash of salt.” Leo grabbed the salt shaker and disappeared. Grandma heard the back door slam and looked out the kitchen window.
Leo was running full speed around the backyard with the salt shaker. “I'm dashing, Grandma!”

Grandpa has played cards every Friday night for fifty years. He shuffles so slowly that the grandkids could eat a whole sandwich between each shuffle. Little Mia finally asked Grandma why Grandpa shuffles that way.
Grandma said, “Honey, Grandpa doesn't really shuffle the cards. He just gives them a gentle suggestion.”

Every Saturday, Grandpa and his buddies play dominoes on the back porch. Grandpa slams every domino down so hard that the whole table jumps. Last week he scored fifteen points and slammed it down so hard that the iced tea glasses rattled.
Grandma said, “That's why we eat after the game, not during.”

Little Max taught the family dog to play Go Fish. Every time Max asked the dog, “Do you have any threes?” the dog barked once. Max decided one bark meant “Go Fish.” They played all afternoon on the living room rug.
By supper the dog had won four games in a row. Max said next time he is teaching the dog how to say yes.

The grandkids spent all afternoon setting up five hundred dominoes in a long, winding line across the living room floor. They planned to knock them over together when Grandma came home. Just as she pulled into the driveway, the cat strolled in.
The cat tapped the first one with her paw. The kids said she just wanted to help with the hard part.

We played Uno with Grandpa on Sunday afternoon. Little Lily played a Draw Four card on him three times in a row. Grandpa's pile of cards got so big he had to hold them with both hands and his chin. He looked at Lily over the top of the pile.
Grandpa said, “That's it. I'm writing you out of my cookie recipe.”

Every Sunday after church, Grandpa plays solitaire at the kitchen table. Little Henry pulled up a chair to watch. After a while, Grandpa sighed and shuffled the cards up to start over. Henry patted him on the shoulder to cheer him up.
Henry said, “It's okay, Grandpa. Even I've never seen anybody lose to themselves before.”

On a road trip to Grandma's, the kids asked “Are we there yet?” about every five minutes. Finally Dad made a new rule: whoever asked next had to count every single cow they passed until they got there. The car was quiet for two whole hours.
Then little Sam said, “Four hundred and twelve. Are we there yet?”

Dad refused to use the GPS on our family road trip. He said he knew a shortcut. An hour later, we pulled into the same little gas station for the third time that afternoon. Dad went inside to buy snacks and act like that was the plan.
The clerk waved and said, “Welcome back! You want your usual?”

We packed the van for a week at the lake: suitcases, coolers, fishing poles and three bikes. Forty-five minutes down the highway, Mom asked, “Did we forget anything?” Everybody said no. Then she turned around and counted heads.
We turned around and drove home. The dog was sitting in the driveway with his leash in his mouth, waiting.

Dad loves to stop at every historical marker on our road trips. He pulls over, reads the whole sign out loud, and takes a picture. By the end of the trip, we could recite every battle, every old mill and every bridge in three states.
Mom said that's why it took nine hours to drive four.

On the way to the beach, little Ava asked Dad why seagulls only fly over the sea. Dad scratched his head, kept his eyes on the road, and said he wasn't sure. Then Grandpa leaned forward from the back seat with a big grin.
Grandpa said, “Because if they flew over the bay, they'd be bagels.”

We went to the county fair, and our neighbor Mr. Wilson entered the scarecrow contest. His scarecrow had a straw hat, overalls and a big grin, and he worked on it for two months. At the end of the day, the judges handed him the blue ribbon.
When we asked why it won, Mr. Wilson said, “He's outstanding in his field.”

We spent the whole day at the beach. The kids built sandcastles, collected shells, and chased the waves back and forth for hours. At sunset, little Emma looked out at the water and asked Grandpa what the ocean said to the shore.
Grandpa said, “Nothing, honey. It just waved.”

On our road trip, the car hit a pothole and we got a flat tire on a little country road. Dad got out, looked at the tire, and found a big shiny fork stuck right in it. He held it up for everybody to see.
Grandpa said, “Well, I told you there was going to be a fork in the road.”

Our family went to the zoo, and little Owen stopped in front of the bear cage. He looked a long time at an old brown bear who was sleeping with his mouth open. Then he turned to Dad and said the bear didn't have a single tooth.
Dad said, “Well, son, that makes him a gummy bear.”
Grandpa took up golf when he retired. Before every round, he packs two pairs of pants in his golf bag. One day his friend finally asked him why he always brought an extra pair along.
Grandpa said, “In case I get a hole in one.”

In the school play, little Ben was supposed to sing a solo as a pony. But the morning of the show, his voice was scratchy from cheering at his sister's ball game. The teacher asked him what was wrong, and he whispered his answer.
Ben whispered, “I can't sing today, Mrs. Lee. I'm a little hoarse.”

Our teacher said the class could have a party on Friday. She asked us to bring snacks, and little Nate asked her if he could bring his homework as a snack, too. She looked very confused and asked him why.
Nate said, “You told us this week's homework would be a piece of cake.”

Little Noah asked his grandpa why there were two big doors on the side of the barn but just one little door on the doghouse. Grandpa didn't know. So Noah asked the next best question he could think of: why do cows wear bells?
Grandpa said, “Because their horns don't work.”

Little Ruby asked her dad a riddle at supper. She said, “What has four wheels and flies?” Dad guessed an airplane, then a helicopter, then a bird with roller skates. Ruby giggled and shook her head every time.
Ruby said, “A garbage truck!” Dad laughed so hard he had to set down his fork.

We went out to eat for Grandpa's birthday, and the waiter brought chips with a big bowl of cheese dip. Little Josh grabbed the bowl and pulled it in front of his plate. Grandpa asked if he could have some of that cheese.
Josh said, “Sorry, Grandpa. That's nacho cheese.”

Little Lucy was struggling with her math homework at the kitchen table. She had a whole page of problems and was getting frustrated. Grandma came in, sat down beside her and asked why the math book looked so sad.
Lucy said, “Because it's got too many problems, Grandma. Just like me.”
Our teacher asked us why we thought fish were so smart. Some kids said it was because they eat a lot of seafood. Some said it was because they swim all day. Then little Jacob raised his hand.
Jacob said, “Because they live in schools.”
Little Tommy came to school one morning carrying a big wooden ladder. The teacher asked him what in the world he needed a ladder for in second grade. Tommy set it down and dusted off his hands.
Tommy said, “Mom said I need to start getting ready for high school.”

Our class went to the dairy farm on a field trip. The farmer showed us the cows and told us about the one that got lots of treats and attention. Then he asked if anyone knew what you get from a cow that's spoiled.
Little Ava said, “Spoiled milk!” The farmer gave her a lollipop for that one.

Little Hank threw the kitchen clock out the window. Mom came running in and asked what in the world he thought he was doing. Hank looked out the window at the clock lying in the grass and seemed a little disappointed.
Hank said, “I just wanted to see time fly.”

The school janitor was cleaning the supply closet when a whole class walked by on the way to recess. He jumped out of the closet with his arms full of paper towels and mops to say hello. The kids all screamed and laughed.
The janitor shouted, “SUPPLIES!”

Grandpa asked the grandkids a riddle at the supper table. He said, “How many months have twenty-eight days?” Everybody said February, of course. Some said February every four years, and some said just February.
Grandpa grinned and said, “All of them. Every month has twenty-eight days.”

A lady walked into the doctor's office and said, “Doctor, I think I'm a moth.” The doctor said, “You don't need a doctor, ma'am. You need a counselor.” She agreed with him. Then he asked why she came to his office instead.
She said, “Well, the light was on.”

Grandpa went to the doctor because his right knee hurt. The doctor examined him and said, “I'm afraid that just comes with age.” Grandpa thought about that for a second, then pointed at his other knee.
Grandpa said, “Well, this one's the same age, and it doesn't hurt a bit.”
Little Tim went to the dentist for his checkup. He sat down in the big chair, and the dentist asked him if he knew what time it was. Tim looked around the room for a clock but couldn't find one.
The dentist smiled and said, “It's tooth-hurty. Time for your checkup.”

Grandpa took his old bicycle to the bike shop because it kept falling over in the garage. The mechanic looked it over, checked the kickstand and spun the wheels. Then he told Grandpa exactly what was wrong with it.
He said, “Nothing's wrong, sir. It's just two tired.”

A frog took his car to the mechanic because it broke down on the highway. The mechanic looked under the hood and said it would take a few days to fix. The frog asked him how he was supposed to get it home in the meantime.
The mechanic said, “Don't worry. We'll have it toad.”

Our dog loves to lie in the sun on the back porch. But on the hottest day of July, he got up and moved under the big oak tree in the shade. Little Mia asked Dad why the dog moved out of his favorite sunny spot.
Dad said, “He didn't want to be a hot dog.”

Little Josh got lost at the zoo for about five minutes. When Dad found him, Josh was standing in front of the leopard exhibit. Josh said he'd been playing hide and seek with the leopard, but he kept winning every round.
Josh said, “It's easy. He's always spotted.”

Grandpa likes to tell people about all the jobs he had before he retired. He worked at a bank, a calendar factory and an orange juice plant. When the grandkids asked why he left each one, he had a different answer every time.
Bank: lost interest. Calendar factory: took a few days off. Orange juice: couldn't concentrate.
Our family was eating at a fancy restaurant for Mom's birthday. Dad told the waiter he heard there was a new restaurant opening on the moon. The waiter asked what Dad thought of it.
Dad said, “I hear the food's great, but there's no atmosphere.”

Little Ben asked Grandpa to help him build a birdhouse. Grandpa got out his toolbox, a stack of wood and a box of nails. Ben asked him what one wall of the birdhouse said to the other wall when they were finished.
Grandpa said, “I'll meet you at the corner.”

Little Ellie's teacher asked the class what a penguin would use to build a house. Some kids said ice, some said snow, and one kid said he would just use bricks like everyone else. Ellie raised her hand.
Ellie said, “He'd igloo it together.”

The music teacher brought a ladder to choir practice and set it right next to the piano. One of the kids asked her what she needed a ladder for in the music room. She climbed up two steps and smiled at the class.
She said, “I need to reach the high notes.”

The janitor at our school was late to work one morning. The principal asked him what happened, because he was always the first one there. The janitor scratched his head and said it was a tough morning, and his broom felt the same way.
The janitor said, “I'm sorry. My broom overswept.”

Dad and I were at the hardware store when he picked up a book about gravity. He started reading it in the checkout line and kept on reading in the parking lot. Mom asked him to put it down and help load the truck.
Dad said, “I can't. It's about anti-gravity. Impossible to put down.”

Our mailman was dropping off a package when Grandpa stopped him to ask a riddle. Grandpa said, “What starts with E, ends with E and only has one letter in it?” The mailman scratched his head and couldn't figure it out.
Grandpa pointed at the mail bag and said, “An envelope!” The mailman laughed all the way to the next house.

Grandpa found a nice smooth stick on our walk through the woods. He held it up and asked the grandkids, “What's brown and sticky?” They guessed candy, honey, maple syrup and peanut butter. Grandpa shook his head at every answer.
Grandpa held it higher and said, “A stick!”

Little Max threw his new boomerang across the park and waited for it to come back. He waited and waited. It never came back, and finally he walked over and picked it up out of the grass. Dad asked him what you call a boomerang that doesn't come back.
Max said, “A stick. I just paid ten dollars for a stick.”

On a long road trip, a big ripe tomato rolled out of the grocery bag and was way behind the rest of the vegetables. The mama tomato turned around and called to the little tomato. Little Ruby asked Dad what the mama tomato said.
Dad said, “Ketchup!”

Grandpa told little Jake that he found a train that only carries bubble gum. Jake didn't believe him and asked what you would even call a train like that. Grandpa leaned over and told him in a whisper.
Grandpa said, “A chew-chew train.”

Our farmer neighbor said he needed to count all his cows before winter. Little Owen asked how he could ever count so many cows without getting mixed up. The farmer pulled something out of his overalls pocket.
The farmer said, “With a cow-culator.”
Our chickens started a band in the back yard. Little Sophie told Dad they'd been practicing all week. Dad asked what instrument the rooster played in this band of chickens.
Sophie said, “The drums, of course. He's got the drumsticks.”
Little Abby asked Grandpa why he always wears a belt made of watches. Grandpa said it was a gift from Grandma, and he looked down at his belt proudly. Abby asked what you call a belt made of watches.
Grandpa said, “A waist of time. But don't tell your Grandma I said that.”

Little Sam's teacher asked him, “Why was six afraid of seven?” Sam said he didn't know. The teacher said it was because seven, eight, nine. Sam thought about it, then asked his own question to the class the next day.
Sam asked, “Then why did seven eat nine?” Nobody knew. Sam said, “Because you're supposed to eat three square meals.”

The doctor saw a banana come into his office looking very sick. The banana said it had been feeling bad all week, and it didn't know what was wrong. The doctor looked at the banana closely and nodded.
The banana said, “I just haven't been peeling well.”

Our neighbor's cookie came to the doctor's office. It said it had been feeling bad for days, ever since it fell off the plate at the church potluck. The doctor asked the cookie how it was feeling now.
The cookie said, “Crummy, Doc. Just crummy.”
Dad's computer was acting funny, so he brought it to the computer doctor. The man looked it over and plugged it in, then pulled up the screen. Dad asked him if it was something serious.
The man said, “Yep. It caught a virus. Make sure it gets plenty of rest.”

Grandma asked Grandpa to clean out the gutters before the fall rains. Grandpa got out the ladder, looked at the gutters for a long time, and then sat down on the porch swing. Grandma asked why he wasn't climbing up there.
Grandpa said, “I don't trust ladders. They're always up to something.”

Dad was in the hardware store buying shovels. The clerk said, “Did you know the shovel was a real groundbreaking invention?” Dad laughed so hard he decided to buy two. On the way out, the clerk added one more thing.
The clerk said, “Come back anytime. We dig customers like you.”

Little Leah walked into the kitchen and found a dozen eggs on the counter, all in a row. She asked Mom why eggs never tell each other jokes. Mom said she didn't know, but she was sure Leah would tell her.
Leah said, “Because they'd crack each other up!”
We were eating spaghetti at Grandma's house. Little Owen held up one long noodle that was made of rubber, a toy he'd hidden on his plate. Grandma asked what in the world you call a fake noodle.
Owen said, “An impasta!” Grandma laughed so hard she had to take off her glasses.
Grandma taught the grandkids how to fix a broken tomato in her garden. She said you need just the right thing. The kids asked what it was. She smiled and handed them a can from her kitchen pantry.
Grandma said, “Tomato paste, of course.”

At the family picnic, one paper plate turned to the other plate on the table. The kids all leaned in to hear what it would say. Little Grace stood up and told everyone exactly what she thought it said.
Grace said, “Lunch is on me!”
Dad was pouring a glass of orange juice when the carton suddenly stopped. He shook it, tipped it over and looked inside. Little Max asked Dad why the orange stopped running.
Dad said, “It ran out of juice.”
Little Sophie found a banana on the counter and couldn't open it. She asked Dad what kind of key opens a banana. Dad thought about house keys, car keys and the key to the shed. Then Sophie told him.
Sophie said, “A monkey!”
The weather was so hot at the ballpark that every fan in the stadium got up and went home early. The announcer said the stadium felt hotter than ever after the game. Grandpa explained why.
Grandpa said, “Because all the fans left.”
Our dog started taking dance lessons in the backyard with the kids. He hopped and wiggled and tried his best, but he just couldn't keep the beat. Little Leo asked Dad why dogs make such bad dancers.
Dad said, “Because they've got two left feet.”
Little Rosie asked Grandpa what kind of shoes frogs wear to church. Grandpa said frogs probably wear their best Sunday shoes like everyone else. Rosie giggled and shook her head.
Rosie said, “No, Grandpa. Open-toad shoes!”
Grandma keeps bees out back by her garden. Little Abby asked her why the bees always have such sticky hair. Grandma looked at the hive and then at Abby with a big smile.
Grandma said, “Because they use honeycombs.”
Our class planned a party in space for science day. We hung paper planets from the ceiling and made a cardboard rocket. The teacher asked how you organize a party in outer space.
Little Jack shouted, “You planet!”
Little Mia asked Grandpa what kind of tree fits in your hand. Grandpa said maybe a tiny bonsai tree, or a seed. Mia laughed and held up her hand, wiggling her fingers in front of his face.
Mia said, “A palm tree, Grandpa!”
Dad took the family camping by the lake. In the morning, he found a big bull asleep by the fence in the pasture next door. Little Jake asked what you call a bull that's sleeping.
Dad said, “A bulldozer.”
Little Ben asked his teacher why the cow crossed the road. The teacher said she knew the answer to the chicken one, but not the cow one. Ben was very proud he had a joke she didn't know.
Ben said, “To get to the udder side!”

In math class, the number zero looked over at the number eight. Eight was all dressed up for picture day, with a nice shirt and a belt cinched around the middle. Little Ruby asked what zero said to eight.
Ruby said, “Nice belt!”
Little Nate asked Dad what you call a dinosaur that's sleeping. Dad guessed a T-Rex in pajamas, then a sleepy-saurus. Nate laughed and shook his head and made a big snoring sound.
Nate said, “A dino-snore!”
Grandpa asked the grandkids a riddle: “What has hands but can't clap?” They guessed a scarecrow, a statue and a glove. Grandpa shook his head at every one.
Grandpa pointed at the wall and said, “The clock!”
Our neighbor brought his alligator to the school pet day. He had dressed the alligator in a little detective vest for the occasion. Little Ella asked what you call an alligator in a vest.
Ella said, “An investigator!”
Dad asked Grandpa what you call a factory that makes products that are just okay. Grandpa scratched his chin and said he worked at one of those for twenty years. Dad laughed.
Grandpa said, “A satisfactory.”
The cows down the road always leave the barn on Saturday night. Little Owen asked Grandpa where in the world the cows go every weekend. Grandpa winked.
Grandpa said, “To the moo-vies.”
A big sunflower in Grandma's garden looked down at a little flower that was just starting to bloom. Little Emma asked Grandma what the big flower said to the little one.
Grandma said, “Hi, bud!”
Grandpa asked the kids why the oysters at the seafood shop wouldn't share their pearls with anyone. The kids guessed that pearls were too expensive. Grandpa shook his head and smiled.
Grandpa said, “Because they're shellfish.”
Little Hank's teacher asked how trees get on the internet. The class guessed by phone, by tablet, and by using the library computer. Hank raised his hand with the answer.
Hank said, “They log in!”
At supper Grandpa asked us what kind of car an egg drives. We guessed a chicken coupe, a pickup truck and a hatchback. Grandpa laughed and shook his head at every single one of our guesses.
Grandpa said, “A Yolkswagen.”
Little Ava asked Dad what elevator jokes are like. Dad said he didn't know any elevator jokes. Ava said it was okay, she'd tell him one, and he'd love it.
Ava said, “They're great, Dad. They work on so many levels.”
Dad said, “I don't like Velcro.” We asked him why, since he wears Velcro shoes on Saturdays. Dad put his feet up and said he thinks the whole thing is a scam.
Dad said, “It's just a big rip-off.”

Our math teacher was late to class one morning. When she finally walked in, we asked her what took so long, because she's never late. She said she couldn't find a parking space, so she came another way.
She said, “I took the rhombus.”

Grandma asked Grandpa if he'd fixed the leaky faucet in the kitchen like he promised. Grandpa said he worked on it all morning and was very proud. Grandma turned it on and water sprayed straight up to the ceiling.
Grandpa said, “Well, it's not leaking anymore. It's a fountain now.”
Dad went to the hardware store to buy a new ladder. The clerk asked if he wanted a six-foot ladder or an eight-foot ladder. Dad said he wasn't sure. The clerk asked what he needed it for.
Dad said, “Mostly to reach the top shelf of the pantry where Mom hides the cookies.”
Our dog loves to ride in the truck with Dad. Every morning he jumps into the driver's seat and waits. Dad has to move him over every single time before he can get in.
Mom says he's just practicing for when he gets his license.
Little Grace asked Dad why the scarecrow in the cornfield never got hungry. Dad said maybe because he's made of straw. Grace said no, there was a much better reason.
Grace said, “Because he's always stuffed!”
The kids asked Grandpa why the man put his money in the freezer. Grandpa said maybe he wanted to keep it fresh. Little Owen shook his head and told him.
Owen said, “He wanted cold, hard cash!”
Little Mia asked Grandma what's the best thing about living in Switzerland. Grandma said the mountains, the chocolate and the cheese. Mia nodded and added one more thing.
Mia said, “And the flag is a big plus.”
Our teacher asked us what a tornado's favorite game is. Some kids said tag, others said hide and seek. Then little Jacob spun around in a circle three times and fell down.
Jacob said, “Twister!”
Grandpa asked the grandkids a riddle about the calendar. He said, “Can February March?” The grandkids thought about it and said no. Grandpa nodded and smiled.
Grandpa said, “No, but April May.”
Little Lucy asked Mom why the bicycle couldn't find its way home from the park. Mom said maybe it forgot the address. Lucy laughed and said that wasn't it at all.
Lucy said, “Because it lost its bearings!”
Our dog dug a big hole in the backyard right in the middle of Mom's flower garden. Mom came out and asked him what he was doing. The dog sat down and wagged his tail, covered in dirt.
Dad said, “He's not digging, honey. He's just planting a bone tree.”
Little Josh asked Dad why it's so hard to keep a secret on a farm. Dad thought about it and said maybe because there are so many animals. Josh grinned.
Josh said, “Because the potatoes have eyes, the corn has ears and the beanstalk.”
Our cat loves to sleep on the warm laptop keyboard. One day Mom found a page full of letters typed across the screen. Dad asked if the cat had been writing a novel.
Mom said, “No, but she did order three bags of cat treats.”
Grandpa took the grandkids to the auto parts store. Little Ben asked the clerk why the car battery was always so cheerful. The clerk didn't know, so Ben told him.
Ben said, “Because it's always positive!”
Mom asked little Leo to set the table for supper. Leo put out the plates, cups and napkins, then stood back proudly. Mom noticed there were no forks or spoons anywhere.
Leo said, “We're having pizza, Mom. I'm just helping you save on dishes.”

Grandma asked Grandpa to pick up eggs, milk and bread from the store. He came back two hours later with a shovel, a new hammer, three kinds of birdseed and a hose. Grandma asked where the groceries were.
Grandpa said, “I got lost in the hardware store on the way there. I'll go back for the eggs tomorrow.”
We played Rook with Grandma and Grandpa until late on Friday night. Grandma won every single hand. Grandpa finally threw down his cards and asked how in the world she kept doing it.
Grandma said, “Fifty years of watching your face, dear. You smile every time you get a good card.”

The grandkids played the game Spoons with Grandma at the kitchen table. The kids thought they'd be faster than her for sure. But every single round, Grandma grabbed the first spoon before anyone else even noticed.
Grandma said, “Honey, I raised five kids. I've been grabbing spoons faster than anybody for forty years.”
What did Noah say while loading the ark?
Now I herd everything!
What kind of lights did Noah use on the ark?
Floodlights.
Which animal on the ark was always peeking at the answers?
The cheetah.
Which animals on the ark had the highest intelligence?
The giraffes.
What did Noah call his weather report?
Forty days of scattered showers.
Who was the smartest man in the Bible?
Abraham. He knew a Lot.
Who was the shortest man in the Bible?
Nehemiah. Some folks call him Knee-high-miah.
How do we know Peter was a wealthy fisherman?
By his net income.
How did Moses make his coffee?
Hebrews it.
What was Moses' favorite hairstyle?
A part down the middle.
What pasta did the Israelites eat in the desert?
Manna-cotti.
Who was the first person in the Bible with a tablet?
Moses. He downloaded it from the cloud.
Why didn't Jonah trust the ocean?
He knew there was something fishy about it.
Who was the greatest banker in the Bible?
Pharaoh's daughter. She drew a little prophet from the Nile bank.
What was David's favorite instrument?
The harp. He was the original lyre-ic writer.
Why was Goliath so easy to find?
He always stood out in a crowd.
What's the Bible's greatest playlist?
Psalms. A hundred and fifty tracks and no skips.
Which Bible book is the best at math?
Numbers, of course.
Which book of the Bible is always on the move?
Exodus. It just can't stay put.
Which Bible book is best at making decisions?
Judges.
Which Bible book would make the best movie?
Acts. It's full of action.
Which Bible book sounds like a sneeze?
Habakkuk. Bless you!
Which Bible book is best for career advice?
Job, of course.
Which Bible book is the first one up every morning?
Genesis. It always gets things started.
Who in the Bible had no parents?
Joshua, son of Nun.
Why didn't Jonah ever get lost at sea?
He had a whale of a sense of direction.
What did the whale say after spitting Jonah out?
You can't keep a good man down!
Why was Adam such a good gardener?
He had the original green thumb.
Who was the first person to name a pet?
Adam. He named every animal there was.
What's the best way to read the third Gospel?
Take a good long Luke.
What did the pastor say when his sermon ran long?
Finally... and lastly... and one more thing...
Why do some folks sit in the back pew?
To get first dibs at the potluck.
What did the casserole say at the church potluck?
I'm just here to be served.
How do you know you're at a church potluck?
Nine kinds of casserole and one lonely salad.
What's a pastor's favorite dessert?
Angel food cake.
What does a dog sing in the church choir?
Anything by Bach.
Why did the hymnal feel so loved?
Everyone kept turning to it.
Why are choir robes so long?
To hide the fuzzy slippers.
What do you call a sheep in the choir?
A baa-ritone.
What cookie does the church choir like best?
Hymn-gersnaps.
What do you call a cat that comes to church every week?
A purr-ishioner.
What's every kid's favorite part of VBS?
Snack time. Everything else is a close second.
Why do VBS songs stick in your head all week?
They come with hand motions.
What's the most-wished-for thing on Sunday morning?
A parking spot close to the door.
How many pizzas does a youth group need?
Just one more.
How did Noah keep the ark running so smoothly?
He had plenty of Noah-how.
What was the last animal off the ark?
The elephant. It was still packing its trunk.
Why couldn't the kangaroos sit still on the ark?
They kept hopping to the window.
How did the snails make it onto the ark in time?
They started walking a year early.
Why did Noah keep a close eye on the termites?
One snack and the whole ark was in trouble.
Why did the two owls get along so well on the ark?
They thought each other was a hoot.
What did the cows do for fun on the ark?
Watched moo-vies.
Why were the fish so calm during the flood?
They didn't need a ticket for the ark.
What did the dove say when it found dry land?
Olive this place!
Why did Moses need a big backpack?
Two stone tablets don't fit in a pocket.
What did the Israelites call the Red Sea crossing?
A shore thing.
Why was Joseph so easy to spot in a crowd?
That coat of many colors.
Why did Joseph love taking naps?
His dreams always came true.
What did Daniel's lions do all night?
Nothing much. Their mouths stayed shut.
Who would be best at waiting in the potluck line?
Job. Nobody has more patience.
Why did Zacchaeus climb the sycamore tree?
He wanted the best seat at the parade.
What did the disciples say when they caught a big one?
Holy mackerel!
Why were the disciples so good at fishing?
They knew how to net-work.
Which Bible book gives the best advice?
Proverbs. It has a saying for everything.
Why are proverbs so short?
Solomon was wise enough to keep it brief.
Why did the pastor bring a pencil to church?
To draw the sermon to a close.
Why are ushers great at hide and seek?
They know every seat in the house.
Where do sheep go for good advice?
To their pasture.
Why did the cow go to church?
To hear the moo-sic.
Why did the tomato go to church?
To ketchup with friends.
What's the strongest thing in the fellowship hall?
The coffee. It could hold up the steeple.
Why are church pews so hard?
To help the congregation stay awake.
Who was the first person to nod off during a long sermon?
Eutychus. Paul preached past midnight.
Why do church bulletins make great paper airplanes?
Ask any kid during a long sermon.
What did the offering plate say to the dollar?
So glad you could make it today!
Why did the church finally get Wi-Fi?
To improve its connection with the youth group.
What's the church organist's favorite workout?
Pulling out all the stops.
Why did the hymnbook look so tired?
It was all sung out.
Which hymn do dentists love?
Crown Him with Many Crowns.
Which hymn do weather forecasters love?
There Shall Be Showers of Blessing.
Which hymn do bakers love?
When the Roll Is Called Up Yonder.
Which hymn do electricians love?
This Little Light of Mine.
Which hymn do sailors love?
Will Your Anchor Hold.
Which hymn do bankers love?
Count Your Blessings.
Which hymn do gardeners love?
In the Garden.
Which hymn do builders love?
The Church's One Foundation.
Which hymn do mountain climbers love?
Higher Ground.
Which hymn do lighthouse keepers love?
Let the Lower Lights Be Burning.
Which hymn do farmers love?
Bringing in the Sheaves.
Which hymn do fishermen love?
Shall We Gather at the River.
Which hymn do pilots love?
I'll Fly Away.
Who was the first carpenter in the Bible?
Noah. He built a boat before it was cool.
Who threw the loudest parade in the Bible?
Joshua. The walls couldn't take it.
What did Jonah's family say when he came home?
Whale, whale, look who's back!
Why was Jonah a great tour guide?
He'd been inside the biggest attraction in the sea.
Why was Gideon's army so small?
Too many got held up at the water fountain.
Why did Balaam's donkey win a speech award?
It had the most surprising line in Numbers.
What's the best kid's lunch in the Bible?
Five loaves and two fish. Plenty to share.
Why did the Sunday school kid bring a flashlight?
The lesson was Jonah, and it's dark in a whale.
What's a Sunday school teacher's favorite snack?
Goldfish crackers. They go with every Jonah lesson.
What's the secret ingredient at every church potluck?
Cream of mushroom soup.
Why does the Jell-O salad show up at every potluck?
It always wiggles its way in.
Why do preachers love fried chicken?
It's the official bird of Sunday dinner.
What's the best way to wake up a sleepy congregation?
Say, 'And in conclusion...'
What's the fastest part of any church service?
The walk to the fellowship hall when lunch is ready.
Why did Adam name it a hippopotamus?
Because it looked like a hippopotamus.
Who was the oldest man in the Bible?
Methuselah. He had the most candles.
How many candles were on Methuselah's last birthday cake?
969. They had to call the fire department.
Why did the wise men's camels need a nap?
Long trip, heavy gifts.
Why do angels make such great singers?
They've got heavenly range.
Why do shepherds never have trouble sleeping?
Counting sheep is their day job.
Who had the best hair in the Bible?
Samson. Until he met the wrong barber.

A Sunday school teacher asked her class to share something they had learned about Noah. One girl said he built a really big boat. Another said the animals came on two by two. Then a little boy in the back waved his hand like crazy and said he even knew the name of Noah's wife.
'Easy,' he said. 'It was Joan of Ark!'

A Sunday school teacher walked around the room while the kids drew pictures. She stopped by little Emma, who was coloring very hard, and asked what she was drawing. 'A picture of God,' Emma said. The teacher smiled and said, 'But sweetheart, nobody knows what God looks like.'
Emma kept right on coloring and said, 'They will in a minute.'

A pastor told his congregation, 'Next Sunday I'm going to preach about telling the truth. To get ready, please read Mark chapter 17 this week.' The next Sunday he asked everyone who had read it to raise their hand. Almost every hand in the church went up.
He smiled and said, 'Mark only has 16 chapters. Now let's begin.'

During the children's sermon, the pastor said, 'I'm thinking of something that's gray, has a big bushy tail, climbs trees and gathers nuts for the winter. Who knows what it is?' The kids all sat quiet. Finally one little boy slowly raised his hand.
'Well, I know the answer's supposed to be Jesus, but it sure sounds like a squirrel to me.'

A little boy sat watching his dad, the pastor, work on Sunday's sermon at the kitchen table. 'Daddy, how do you know what to say?' he asked. His dad smiled and said, 'I pray about it, and the Lord helps me.' The boy kept watching as his dad scribbled and erased.
'Then how come you keep crossing stuff out?'

A little boy listened closely when the pastor read, 'For dust you are, and to dust you will return.' That afternoon he ran into the kitchen with big eyes. 'Mom! Is it true we come from dust and go back to dust?' 'That's what the Bible says,' she told him.
'Then you'd better look under my bed. Somebody's either coming or going!'

Brother Earl's wife told him to bring something to the church potluck that nobody else would think to bring. He thought about it all week long. On Sunday morning he stopped by the grocery store and walked into the fellowship hall proud as a peacock, carrying his dish.
A bucket of fried chicken. He was the twelfth person through the door with one.

Miss Ruth showed up at church a full hour early every single Sunday, rain or shine. One morning the new pastor finally asked her if she came early to pray or to get the coffee started. She just shook her head and pointed out the window.
'I've had the same parking spot for 32 years, Pastor, and I'm not losing it now.'

One Sunday the pastor noticed a man get up and walk out right in the middle of his sermon. About forty minutes later the man slipped back in, just in time for the closing hymn. After church, the pastor asked him where in the world he had gone.
'To get a haircut.' 'Why not get one before church?' 'I didn't need one before church.'

During a long sermon, the pastor noticed old Mr. Jenkins sound asleep in the third pew. He leaned over the pulpit and quietly asked Mr. Jenkins' little grandson, sitting right beside him, to please wake his grandpa up.
The boy whispered back, 'You put him to sleep, Pastor. You wake him up.'

On the thirty-ninth day of the flood, Mrs. Noah came up to check on her husband. 'The goats are grumpy, the parrots won't hush, and the monkeys got into the bananas again,' she said. 'But the woodpeckers seem real happy.'
Noah said, 'Let's keep them happy. And let's never tell them what this boat is made of.'

A family was visiting a big church for the very first time. When the ushers started down the aisle with the offering plates, the youngest boy watched them come closer and closer. Just as the plate reached their pew, he tugged his daddy's sleeve and whispered loud enough for three rows to hear.
'Don't pay for me, Daddy. I'm under five!'

The church put up a brand new sign in the parking lot right by the front door that said 'Reserved for Visitors.' The very next Sunday, Brother Jim, who had come to that church every week for forty years, pulled right into it. A young usher hurried over to tell him the spot was for visitors.
'I know, son,' Brother Jim said. 'I visit every single week.'

On the last day of Vacation Bible School, the director asked the kids what they would remember most. One said the memory verse. Another said the song about Noah. Another said the ark made out of popsicle sticks. Then a little girl in the front row shot her hand up with a big grin.
'The day Pastor Mike got hit with a water balloon!'

The youth pastor promised all the parents that every kid at the lock-in would be asleep by midnight. At 3 a.m. one of the moms stopped by to drop off more snacks. The kids were wide awake, playing hide and seek all over the fellowship hall.
The youth pastor was sound asleep under the ping-pong table.

The church secretary was in a big hurry to finish Sunday's bulletin. She typed up the announcements, the prayer list, the potluck sign-up sheet and the choir schedule as fast as she could. One announcement made the whole church chuckle that morning.
'The peacemaking meeting scheduled for Tuesday has been canceled due to a conflict.'

After church, a little girl asked her grandma why the choir sang a song about a teddy bear. Grandma was puzzled and said she didn't remember any song about a bear. So the little girl sang it for her, loud and proud, right there in the parking lot.
'Gladly, the cross-eyed bear!' The hymn was really 'Gladly the Cross I'd Bear.'

A little boy sang his heart out when the congregation sang 'Bringing in the Sheaves.' On the drive home, he looked at his grandma with a puzzled face and said, 'Grandma, I really like that song, but I have one question about it.'
