'Why does the church sing so much about laundry? Bringing in the sheets?'

The Sunday school teacher asked each child to bring something that reminded them of a Bible story. One girl brought two stuffed animals for Noah's ark. A boy brought a smooth rock for David. Another brought a loaf of bread. Then little Caleb walked in carrying his grandpa's fire extinguisher.
'It's for Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego,' he said. 'Just in case.'

In the church CHRISTmas pageant, little Jacob was cast as the innkeeper. He had just one line: 'There is no room in the inn.' He practiced it all week. But when Mary and Joseph finally knocked on his cardboard door, Jacob looked at their sad faces and just couldn't stand it.
'There's no room in the inn... but y'all come on in and have some cookies anyway!'

At the CHRISTmas pageant, the three wise men walked down the aisle carrying their gifts. The first two wore shiny paper crowns. The third little boy wore his granddad's big firefighter helmet. Afterward, his mom asked him why in the world he wore it.
'Because the Bible says the wise men came from afar!'

God brought the animals to Adam one by one to be named. Adam worked hard all day. A tall one with spots became the giraffe. A big gray one with a long nose became the elephant. Then, late in the afternoon, along waddled a furry little creature with a duck's bill, a beaver's tail and webbed feet.
Adam rubbed his eyes and said, 'Platypus. Nobody's going to believe me anyway.'
As the dark clouds rolled in and the first big drops began to fall, Mrs. Noah stood at the door of the ark with a worried look on her face. 'Noah,' she said, 'did you remember to pack the umbrellas?'
Noah patted the side of the boat and said, 'Dear, we ARE the umbrella.'

After Jonah got back to dry land, an old friend asked him how his big trip went. Jonah sighed. 'Well, the boat ride got rough, the crew tossed me overboard, and the hotel I ended up in was a giant fish. Room service was nothing but seaweed for three days.'
'But I'll say this. I finally went where I was told to go.'

A grandpa found his granddaughter frowning over her Bible at the kitchen table. 'What's the matter, sugar?' he asked. 'Grandpa, this chapter is nothing but names. So-and-so begat so-and-so, who begat somebody else. I've counted fourteen begats already.'
'Is this the part of the Bible where they kept the phone book?'

The pastor texted the whole choir: 'Practice moved to 7 tonight. Please bring your hymnals.' He didn't notice that his phone's autocorrect had changed 'hymnals' to 'animals.' That evening, the choir members started arriving at the church.
Mrs. Jenkins came in with her cat, her parakeet and a note: 'Is this a Noah thing?'

A little girl sat next to her great-grandpa in church and asked how long he had been coming there. He smiled and told her he had sat in that very same pew every Sunday for seventy years. Her eyes got as big as saucers.
'Wow, Grandpa! That must have been one really long sermon!'

The Sunday school teacher finished the story of Noah's ark and asked, 'If you were Noah, what's the first thing you would do?' One child said build it extra big. Another said pack lots of snacks. A boy who had spent all summer at the lake had a different idea.
'I'd make sure the two mosquitoes missed the boat.'

A little girl was chosen to recite Psalm 23 in front of the whole church. She walked up to the microphone in her Sunday dress, took a deep breath and began, 'The Lord is my shepherd...' Then she froze. She looked out at all those faces, thought hard for a moment, and finished with a big smile.
'...and that's all I want!' The pastor said it was the best sermon he'd heard all year.

The youth group held a car wash to raise money for summer camp. The pastor pulled his car up first so everyone would see the church supported them. Two hours, forty sponges and one very big water fight later, the pastor came back to pick up his car.
The car was still dusty. But every kid in the youth group was sparkling clean.

A visiting pastor was preaching about the new building fund. Before the service he told the organist, 'At the end, I'll ask everyone who wants to pledge a hundred dollars to stand up. Play something fitting while they do.' The organist nodded and smiled.
When the moment came, the organist played 'The Star-Spangled Banner,' and the whole church stood up.

Grandpa gave little Ella a dollar and a quarter before church. 'Put whichever one you want in the offering plate,' he told her. After the service, he asked her which one she gave. 'The quarter,' she said with a smile.
'Pastor said God loves a cheerful giver, and I was a lot more cheerful giving the quarter.'

The pastor stepped up to the pulpit and announced, 'This morning's sermon is about patience.' Right then the projector froze, the microphone squealed, a baby started crying in the back and somebody's phone began playing a ringtone.
The pastor just smiled and said, 'Well, folks, looks like today is a hands-on lesson.'

When Grandma started watching church online, the family set up her tablet in the living room so she could see the service. That first Sunday morning, they found her dressed in her best church clothes with her Bible in her lap.
She was on the third cushion from the left. Same spot as her pew for thirty years.

During the candlelight service, so many candles were lit that the smoke alarm went off. Within minutes, the volunteer fire department showed up with lights flashing. The chief walked down the aisle, looked around at the whole congregation holding candles, and shook his head.
'Pastor, I know you want this church on fire for the Lord, but let's not take it literally.'

A visiting preacher was getting ready to deliver his first sermon at a small country church. He leaned over to an old deacon and asked, 'Brother, how long would you like me to preach this morning?' The deacon thought for a moment and patted him on the shoulder.
'Preach as long as you like, son. We all leave at noon.'

The children's choir sang 'This Little Light of Mine' for the whole church. When they got to the line 'Hide it under a bushel,' they were all supposed to shout 'No!' Little Sam took his job very, very seriously.
He yelled 'NO!' so loud that Grandpa woke up in the back pew and hollered, 'No what?'

During the lesson on Zacchaeus, the Sunday school teacher asked why he climbed up the sycamore tree. One girl said, 'So he could see Jesus.' A boy said, 'Because he was a wee little man.' Then Tommy, who had climbed the big oak behind the church just last week, raised his hand.
'Because it's the one place your little sister can't follow you.'
es: How do Easter eggs stay in shape?
They do egg-ercises before the big hunt.
Why don't Easter eggs tell secrets?
They might crack up.
How did the Easter egg get to the hunt?
It scrambled over as fast as it could.
What do you call an Easter egg from outer space?
An egg-straterrestrial.
Why did the Easter egg go to school?
To get egg-ucated before the big hunt.
What does a chick say when it finds an Easter egg?
Hey, that looks just like my old house!
Where do Easter eggs go on vacation?
New Yolk City.
What did one Easter egg say to the other?
Heard any good yolks lately?
Why did the Easter egg cross the road?
To get to the other side of the egg hunt.
What did the Easter egg say when the kids finally found it?
Took you long enough! I've been under this bush since sunrise.
How do you find the very last Easter egg?
Wait till summer. The lawn mower always finds it.
Why did Grandma hide the Easter eggs in the vegetable garden?
So the kids would finally go near the broccoli.
Which Easter egg is always found last?
The one Grandpa hid and forgot about.
Why did the plastic Easter egg rattle?
It was full of jellybeans and excitement.
What's the best way to mail an Easter egg?
By egg-spress delivery.
Why did the boy bring a magnifying glass to the Easter egg hunt?
He wasn't missing the tiny jellybean eggs this year.
Why did the kids wear rain boots to the Easter egg hunt?
April showers bring muddy Easter eggs.
What did the Easter egg say to the frying pan?
Not today, pal. I've got an Easter egg hunt to get to!
What's an Easter egg's favorite game?
Hide and go peep.
Why are dyed Easter eggs bad at hide-and-seek?
They're bright pink. Kind of a giveaway.
Why did the Easter egg hide in Grandpa's toolbox?
Nobody but Grandpa ever opens it.
Why did the Easter egg get a gold star?
It was egg-ceptional.
What do you call an Easter egg that sings in the choir?
An egg-cellent soloist.
Why was the Easter egg so tired on Easter morning?
It spent all Saturday night in the dye cups.
Why did the Easter egg hunt need a referee?
The cousins kept yelling 'finders keepers.'
What's yellow, purple and green and hides in the yard on Easter?
An Easter egg that couldn't pick a color.
Why did the Easter egg wear sunglasses?
The sunrise service was too bright.
What did the Easter egg say after it was dyed blue?
I'm feeling a little blue today.
Why did the Easter egg turn green?
It took a dip in the blue dye, then the yellow.
What did the Easter egg say after its turn in the dye cup?
I've never felt so colorful in my life!
How do you make an Easter egg laugh?
Tell it a really good yolk.
Why did the Easter egg have stripes?
Somebody dipped it in three colors at once.
Why do kids love dyeing Easter eggs?
It's the one night Mom says yes to messy fingers.
Why does Mom cover the whole kitchen before we dye Easter eggs?
Last year the cat came out purple.
Why did the Easter egg take an art class?
It wanted to be a masterpiece by Sunday.
What do you call an Easter egg covered in glitter?
The one Grandma will be finding in the carpet till June.
Why did the Easter basket go to the doctor?
It felt empty inside after the kids got to it.
Why is Easter basket grass so hard to clean up?
You'll still be finding it on the Fourth of July.
What did the Easter basket say to the plastic grass?
You're the only filler I'll ever need.
Why did the Easter basket get a promotion?
It could really carry a load.
Why do basketball players love Easter?
They're great at dunking eggs in dye.
What's a basket's favorite day of the year?
Easter. It's the one day everybody wants to hold it.
Why did the jellybean go to church on Easter?
It wanted to be a good bean.
How do jellybeans greet each other on Easter?
Have a sweet one!
What's a jellybean's favorite part of Easter?
Getting picked first out of the basket.
Why did the black jellybean feel left out on Easter?
Grandpa was the only one who ever picked it.
What do you call a melted chocolate Easter egg?
A puddle of happiness.
Why did the chocolate Easter egg go to the doctor?
It was feeling hollow inside.
Why did the chocolate egg stay in the shade at the Easter egg hunt?
It didn't want to have a meltdown.
What do you call a marshmallow chick at Easter sunrise service?
An early peep.
Why did the marshmallow chick sit on the front pew on Easter?
It wanted a good peep at the choir.
What did the marshmallow chick say in the Easter basket?
Don't make a peep. The kids are coming!
What did the baby chick say on Easter morning?
Look at me, I'm finally out of my shell!
Why do chicks love Easter?
It's the one day everybody talks about their family.
What do you call a chick in an Easter basket?
A sweet tweet.
What did the hen say when she saw the dyed Easter eggs?
Who painted my babies purple?
Why did the hen sit in the Easter basket?
She thought it was a really fancy nest.
Why did the rooster get invited to Easter sunrise service?
He's never once been late for a sunrise.
Why are chickens so busy the week before Easter?
Somebody has to supply all those eggs.
What did the hen say to the Easter egg hunters?
Go easy, those are my grandkids.
Why did the chick wear a bonnet on Easter?
It wanted to look egg-stra special.
Why did the chick get in trouble at the Easter egg hunt?
It kept telling everyone where its brothers were hiding.
What did the lamb say on Easter morning?
Happy Easter to ewe!
What did the lamb say when it saw the Easter lilies?
Baa-utiful!
Why did the little lamb wear a bow on Easter?
It wanted to look sharp in its Sunday wool.
Why are lambs great at Easter egg hunts?
They never get sheepish about looking under bushes.
What's a lamb's favorite Easter treat?
A baa-sket full of candy.
Why did the spring lamb eat the Easter basket grass?
It looked greener than the pasture.
Why is Easter sunrise service so early?
So nobody can say the sun beat them to church.
What did the sun say at Easter sunrise service?
Glad y'all could make it this early!
Why did Grandpa bring a lawn chair to Easter sunrise service?
He planned to watch the sun come up, then rest his eyes.
How do you get a teenager to Easter sunrise service?
Tell them there's breakfast after.
What's the hardest part of Easter sunrise service?
Finding your shoes in the dark at 5 a.m.
Why did the alarm clock go to Easter sunrise service?
It wanted credit for getting everybody there.
Why was the coffee pot so popular at Easter sunrise service?
It was the only one up before the pastor.
Why do people bring jackets to Easter sunrise service?
Spring mornings never got the memo that it's spring.
Why did the birds sing at Easter sunrise service?
They heard the choir needed a warm-up act.
Why does the choir hum at Easter sunrise service?
It's too early to remember the words.
What's the best part of Easter sunrise service?
The pancake breakfast right after.
Why did Dad set three alarms the night before Easter?
Sunrise service waits for no one.
Why do Easter lilies make great band members?
They're shaped like little trumpets.
What did the Easter lily say to the usher?
Thanks for the front-row seat!
Why does Grandpa sit far from the Easter lilies?
One sniff and he sneezes through the whole sermon.
Why do Easter lilies always look so calm?
They know they've got the best seats in church.
What do Easter lilies do after church?
They go home with whoever ordered them.
What did the Easter lily say to the tulip?
Don't feel bad. I only get the stage once a year.
Why did the Easter lily get stage fright?
The whole church was looking its way.
What do you call a lily that can't wait for Easter?
A real blooming fan.
Why did the little girl twirl all through Easter service?
Her new Easter dress was made for spinning.
What's the hardest thing about wearing your Sunday best on Easter?
Keeping it clean through the egg hunt.
Why did the Easter bonnet go to church early?
To get a seat where everyone could see it.
Why did Grandma's Easter hat need its own pew?
It had more flowers than the altar.
Why did the boy wear sneakers with his Easter suit?
He was planning to win the egg hunt.
What's the first rule of wearing white on Easter?
Eat the chocolate egg after the pictures.
Why do families take Easter pictures before church?
After the egg hunt, nobody is clean.
Why did Dad's Easter tie have a jellybean stuck to it?
He was saving it for later.
What do you call an Easter bonnet with a bird on top?
A hat with its own choir.

Why do deviled eggs wear paprika on Easter?

Why do kids love Palm Sunday?

What do you call a Palm Sunday palm that tells jokes?

What did one Palm Sunday palm say to the other?

Why was the palm branch tired after Palm Sunday?

What does a palm tree do on Palm Sunday?
Takes the day off and lets its branches do the waving.
Why do kids love the week after Palm Sunday?

Why did the boy keep his Palm Sunday palm all week?
So he could wave it at the Easter ham.
What did the Palm Sunday palm say to the Easter lily?
I opened the show last week. Your turn!
Why are church parking lots so full on Easter?

Why did the usher bring extra chairs on Easter?
The pews were packed like an egg carton.
Why does the choir love Easter so much?
They finally get to sing the big songs.
Why do church pews feel smaller on Easter?
Big bonnets and even bigger dresses.
Why does the organist stretch her fingers before Easter?
It's the biggest playing day of the year.
What's the second loudest sound in church on Easter?
Candy wrappers. The choir is first.
Why did the kids sit in the front pew on Easter?
To be first out the door for the egg hunt.
Why did the pastor wear sneakers under his Easter robe?
He was judging the egg hunt right after the last amen.
What does the Sunday school class do on Easter?
Count the minutes till the egg hunt.
Why did the church kitchen smell so good on Easter?
The ladies had been baking since Thursday.
What do you call an Easter potluck at church?
A ham-boree.
Why do church greeters smile extra big on Easter?
They get to meet everybody's cousins.
Why did the church nursery need extra helpers on Easter?
Every grandbaby in town was visiting.
Why did the kids fold the bulletin into an Easter bonnet?
The announcements were running long.
Why did the Easter bunny go to the barber?
He was having a bad hare day.
How does the Easter bunny stay fit?
Lots of hare-obics.
What did the Easter bunny say when he showed up late?
Sorry, I hopped as fast as I could!
How does the Easter bunny keep his fur so neat?
With a hare brush.
What's the Easter bunny's favorite restaurant?
IHOP.
Why is the Easter bunny so good at hiding eggs?

What do you call the Easter bunny on vacation?
A hoppy camper.
Why does Easter weather wear three outfits?
Sunshine, rain and a jacket, all before the egg hunt.
Why do the flowers bloom right before Easter?

Why did the tulip go to the Easter egg hunt?
It heard there would be a lot of colors there.
What did the robin say on Easter morning?
Hey, who copied my egg color?
Why don't Easter eggs drive the church van?

Why did the Easter egg hunt go into overtime?

Why was the hard-boiled Easter egg so calm?
It had a tough shell and a soft heart.
What's an Easter egg's least favorite day of the week?
Fry-day.
What do you call an Easter egg that loves the outdoors?
A free-range hider.
What do Easter eggs say to stay cheerful?
Always look on the sunny side up.
What did the egg carton say the night before Easter?
All twelve of my kids get their colors tonight!
Why was the egg carton sad on Easter Monday?

What do you call the Easter egg Dad dropped while hiding it?

Why did the toddler win the Easter egg hunt?

Why did Grandma hide all the Easter eggs at knee height?
So the little ones could win and the big ones could help.
What did the Easter egg say to the grass?
Grow a little taller, they're getting close!
Why did the Easter egg hunt start late?
Grandpa still had a dozen eggs in his pockets.
Why did the plastic Easter egg roll away?

What did the empty plastic Easter egg say?
Somebody beat you to me!
Why are plastic Easter eggs bad at keeping secrets?

What do you call a plastic Easter egg full of coins?
A piggy bank in disguise.
What's inside Grandpa's plastic Easter eggs?
Butterscotch candies he's had since 1998.
Why did the Easter egg wear a raincoat?

What did the Easter egg say to the flashlight?
Nice try, but I'm under the porch.
What do you call an Easter egg dipped in every color?
Brown. But don't tell the artist.
Why were Dad's fingers purple on Easter morning?
He helped dye the eggs and forgot the spoon.
What's the hardest Easter egg to dye?
The one that rolls off the table first.
What's every kid's favorite Easter egg color?
Whichever one their sister picked.
Why did the Easter egg ask for a second dip?
It wanted to be extra blue.
Why do kids wake up so early on Easter morning?
Those baskets aren't going to find themselves.
What's the first thing kids say on Easter morning?
Is it time to hunt yet?
Why did the boy sleep in his Easter suit?
To save time getting ready for sunrise service.
Why is Easter morning so busy?
Church, eggs, ham and pictures, all before lunch.
Why did the church bells ring extra long on Easter?
They were just as happy as everybody else.
Why did the kids' choir wave at their parents on Easter?
They forgot the words but remembered the waving.
Why did the Sunday school teacher bring jellybeans on Easter?
To keep the class sweet till the egg hunt.
Why did Grandpa's egg win the Easter egg roll?
It found the only hill in the yard.
What did the spoon say in the Easter egg-and-spoon race?
Hold still, I've got you!
Why do Easter eggs make good friends?
They're always there to egg you on.
How do Easter eggs say goodbye?
See you next Easter, if we don't get eaten first!
Why did the duck come to the Easter egg hunt?
It wanted to see what all the quacking was about.
What did the duckling say about Easter?
It's egg-zactly my kind of day.
Why did the goose skip the Easter egg hunt?
It already knew where all the eggs were.
What did the farmer say on Easter morning?
My hens worked overtime this week.
Why do farm kids win every Easter egg hunt?
They've been hunting eggs in the henhouse all year.
Why did the dog love the Easter egg hunt?
He thought every egg was a ball just for him.
Why did the cat sit in the Easter basket?
It fit, so it sat.
What did the dog bring to Easter dinner?
His best begging face for the ham.
Why was the cat so calm on Easter?
It already knew the dog would get blamed for the ham.
Why do church ushers love Easter?
It's the one Sunday they get to use every chair in the building.
Why did the pianist play so fast on Easter?
She could smell the ham from the church kitchen.
What do you call a church van full of kids on Easter?
The egg-spress.
What did the choir robe say on Easter morning?
Finally, my big day!
Why did the Easter program have so many sheep costumes?
Every little lamb in Sunday school wanted a part.
Why did the girl practice her Easter speech in the mirror?
She wanted the mirror to clap first.
What's the best thing about singing in the Easter choir?
You get the best view of the Easter hats.
Why did the children's choir sing so loud on Easter?
They wanted Grandma in the back row to hear every word.
What did Grandma say about the new Easter dresses?
My, my, that's prettier than the lilies.
Why did the boy's Easter tie end up on the dog?
They both wanted to look sharp for the pictures.
What do you call a family in matching Easter outfits?
A walking egg carton.
Why did the Easter bonnet win first prize?
It had flowers, ribbons and a tiny nest on top.
Why does Grandma always make extra deviled eggs at Easter?
She counts the cousins, then counts again.
What's the hardest part of Easter dinner?
Waiting for the blessing while the ham smells that good.
Why did the kids hide the dessert at Easter?
Practice for next year's egg hunt.
What's for lunch the Tuesday after Easter?
Ham. What else?
Why did the carrot cake show up to Easter dinner?
It was the only cake that fit the theme.
Why are deviled eggs always the first thing gone at Easter?
Everyone says they'll have just one.

On Easter Sunday afternoon, Grandpa hid the golden egg so well that after an hour of searching, not one of the grandkids could find it. They finally gave up and begged him for a hint. Grandpa scratched his head, looked around the yard and thought for a long, long time.
Then he said, 'I was kind of hoping one of you would find it, so I'd remember where I put it.'

The family dyed three dozen eggs on Saturday night, and on Easter morning Dad hid every one of them in the backyard. The kids found thirty-five. Everybody searched the rest of the afternoon for the last one, under every bush and behind every flowerpot, but it was nowhere to be found.
In June, Dad came in and said, 'Good news, I found the last Easter egg. Bad news, the lawn mower found it first.'

A little boy asked his grandmother why she wore such a big flowered hat every Easter Sunday. 'Honey, when I was a girl, every lady in church wore an Easter bonnet,' she said. He studied it for a minute and said, 'But Grandma, yours has a bird's nest on it.'
Grandma smiled and said, 'That's how you know it's a good one. Even the birds approved.'

A little boy asked his mom why it was called the Easter sunrise service. 'Because we start right when the sun comes up,' she said. He looked out the window at the dark sky, pulled the blanket up to his chin and gave a great big yawn.
'Then can we ask the sun to come up at ten o'clock like normal people?'

Two eggs were sitting side by side in a pot of hot water the night before the big Easter egg hunt. The water bubbled and steamed, and the kitchen smelled like vinegar from all the dye cups waiting on the table. Finally, the first egg said, 'Whew, it sure is hot in here!'
The second egg jumped and said, 'Wow! A talking egg!'

At Easter dinner, Grandma asked little Sam to say the blessing. Sam looked at the ham, the deviled eggs, the potatoes and the rolls, then looked down the long table full of hungry cousins. He bowed his head and folded his hands nice and tight.
'Thank you for this food, and please help Uncle Ray leave some ham for the rest of us. Amen.'

After the church Easter egg hunt, a little girl walked back with an empty basket. Her mom asked, 'Didn't you find any eggs, sweetheart?' 'I found twelve,' she said proudly. 'Well, where are they?' Mom asked, looking all around.
'I hid them again so I could find them twice!'

Dad decided this was the year he'd dye the Easter eggs all by himself. He read the box, mixed the tablets and lined up the cups on the kitchen table. An hour later the eggs were as pale as could be, but Dad's hands were bright blue, green and purple. Mom asked how it went.
Dad said, 'The eggs didn't take much color, but I'll be the brightest usher at church tomorrow.'

Mom spent twenty minutes getting Tommy into his new Easter suit, a little clip-on tie and shiny black shoes. When he finally looked in the mirror, he frowned. 'What's wrong?' Mom asked. 'You look so handsome!'
'I know, Mom. But how am I supposed to crawl under the bushes at the egg hunt in this?'

Every Easter, Mom vacuums up the plastic basket grass. By May she's found it in the couch, the car and the dog's bed. On the Fourth of July she found a piece in the freezer, and at Thanksgiving there was one stuck to the gravy boat.
Dad says that Easter grass has been to more family dinners than he has.

Grandpa sneezes every time he gets near an Easter lily. This year the flower committee lined fourteen lilies across the front of the church, and Grandpa still insisted on sitting in the very first row. Right in the quietest part of the special song, he let out the biggest sneeze that church had ever heard.
When the song ended, the soloist smiled and said, 'Thank you, Brother Ed. I've never had a harmony that loud.'

After the Easter egg hunt, Grandma counted the grandkids' eggs. The oldest had twenty, the next one had fifteen, and the next one had ten. The youngest, who was barely four, had thirty. 'My goodness,' Grandma said. 'How did you find so many?'
'Easy. I just followed Grandpa around while he was hiding them.'

Aunt June brings deviled eggs to the Easter potluck every single year. This year she made four dozen. By the time she set the platter on the table, half of them were already gone. 'Who ate my deviled eggs?' she asked. Everybody turned and looked at Uncle Earl.
Uncle Earl wiped his mouth and said, 'I was just making sure they were safe to serve.'

Little Emma dipped every one of her Easter eggs in every single color cup. When she pulled them out, they were all the same muddy brown. Her mom said, 'Oh honey, I think you mixed too many colors.' Emma looked at her eggs for a long moment.
'That's okay. I'll just tell everybody they're chocolate eggs.'

After church on Easter, Mom lined the whole family up by the lilies for a picture. Dad blinked. The baby cried. The dog walked right through the middle. Grandpa's eyes were closed in every shot. Forty-two tries later, they finally got one where everyone was smiling.
Then they realized the camera was facing the wrong way, and they had forty-two perfect pictures of Mom.

A little boy came home from Palm Sunday service waving his palm branch. 'What's that for?' Dad asked. 'You wave it when everybody's happy,' the boy said. The next Sunday at Easter dinner, Grandma carried out her famous coconut cream pie, and the boy jumped up and waved his palm as hard as he could.
'See, Dad? Everybody's happy!'

Grandma bought brand-new shoes for Easter Sunday, and they squeaked with every single step. She came in a little late and had to walk all the way down the aisle to the front pew while the church was perfectly quiet. Squeak. Squeak. Squeak.
A little boy in the back whispered, 'Mom, I think Grandma's shoes joined the Easter choir.'

For the Easter egg hunt, Mom filled fifty plastic eggs with jellybeans, and Dad filled fifty more with quarters. Grandpa wanted to help too, so he filled one special golden egg himself. When his grandson finally found it, he popped it open and pulled out a tiny folded note.
It said, 'Congratulations! You've won the job of helping Grandma with the Easter dishes.'

A farmer was telling the folks at church about his rooster. 'Every morning, rain or shine, that bird crows at five o'clock on the dot,' he said. 'Every morning except Easter Sunday. For years I couldn't figure out why he was quiet that one morning a year. This year I finally found out.'
'He was already sitting in the back row at sunrise service.'

The church held an Easter bonnet contest. Mrs. Pearl's hat had silk flowers, satin ribbon, a little bird and a nest with three tiny eggs. It was so tall that the family behind her had to move twice. When the judges finally announced the winner, they apologized for taking so long.
'We'd have picked her sooner,' they said, 'but we couldn't see over her hat to read our scorecards.'

Little Josh had one line in the children's Easter program: 'Look, the flowers are blooming!' He practiced it all week long, at breakfast, in the car and at bedtime. On Easter morning he stepped up to the front, looked out at the whole church, took a deep breath and waved.
'Hi, Grandma! I'm a flower!'

The Monday after Easter, Mom made ham sandwiches. Tuesday was ham and eggs. Wednesday was ham and bean soup. Thursday was ham casserole. On Friday, Dad came home from work and asked, 'What's for supper?' Mom smiled and said, 'Good news, something new!'
'Ham pizza.'

Grandpa set up an Easter egg roll in the backyard. Each grandkid had to push a dyed egg across the grass with a spoon. Grandpa decided to race too. His egg took off down the hill, rolled past the garden, bounced over a tree root and plopped right into the creek.
Grandpa threw up his arms and declared himself the winner, since his egg went the farthest.

The church flower committee met to decide how many Easter lilies to order. One lady said fifty. Another said seventy-five. The chairwoman said a hundred. The pastor raised his hand and asked, 'Will a hundred lilies even fit up front?'
The chairwoman said, 'Pastor, if they don't fit, you'll just have to make the sermon shorter.'

At the church Easter egg hunt, a little boy started crying. 'I lost my basket!' Everybody stopped to look for it. Finally one of the ushers found a basket under the slide, packed full of eggs, and brought it right over. The boy wiped his eyes and looked inside.
'That's not mine. Mine had way more eggs in it.'

The pastor promised a short Easter sermon so everyone could get home to their ham. Halfway through his message, the smell of the church kitchen's breakfast casserole drifted into the sanctuary. The pastor stopped, sniffed the air and looked out at the congregation.
'And that,' he said, 'concludes this morning's message.'

At four o'clock on Easter morning, a little girl tiptoed into her parents' room. 'Is it time to find the eggs?' 'No, honey, go back to sleep.' At four-thirty she came back. At five she came back again. Finally Dad said, 'Sweetheart, it's still dark outside!'
'That's okay, Daddy. I brought a flashlight!'

A little boy asked his dad why families hide eggs on Easter. Dad explained that it's a fun spring tradition. The boy thought about it. 'So the grown-ups hide the eggs, the kids find the eggs, and then the grown-ups take pictures?' Dad said, 'That's right.'
'And then who eats all the chocolate?' Dad said, 'Let's not worry about that part, son.'

A teenager promised his mom he'd go to Easter sunrise service if she woke him up. At five, she knocked. At five-ten, she knocked again. At five-twenty, she flipped on the lights and opened the curtains. He finally rolled over and squinted at her.
'Mom, can you ask the sun to hit snooze one more time?'

Mom bought matching pastel outfits for the family's Easter picture: pink for the girls, light blue for the boys and a mint green tie for Dad. Everyone looked perfect standing in front of the church. Then the dog came running across the yard wearing a bright yellow bow.
Grandma said, 'Well, now we look like a whole carton of Easter eggs.'

Little Mia was in charge of the Easter egg dye this year. She lined up red, yellow, blue and green cups on the table and carefully set out the wire dippers. Then she put an egg in each cup and waited. And waited. After ten minutes, she called out to her mom.
'Mom, how long until they hatch?'

The children's choir practiced their Easter song for six weeks. On Easter morning, they marched up front in their Sunday best. The music started, and every single kid forgot the words at the same time. So they did the only thing they could think of.
They hummed it so loud that Grandma in the back row said it was the best version she'd ever heard.

Uncle Joe told everyone he was going to eat light at Easter dinner this year. Then he had ham, two helpings of potatoes, three deviled eggs, a roll, green beans and a big slice of coconut cake. Aunt Linda looked at his plate and raised an eyebrow.
'What?' Uncle Joe said. 'All of it was light enough for me to lift.'

Grandma asked her grandson what his favorite part of Easter Sunday was. 'The music, the lilies, the egg hunt and the ham,' he said. 'And what about the sermon?' Grandma asked. He thought about it for a second.
'Oh, I liked that too. That's when I rested up for the egg hunt.'

A city boy visited his grandpa's farm the week before Easter. He saw the hens sitting on their nests, and Grandpa showed him how to gather the eggs. The boy carefully held up a plain brown egg and turned it over and over in his hands.
'Grandpa, which hen do I ask for the purple ones?'

Every Easter, Dad insists on carving the ham himself. He puts on his apron, gathers everyone in the kitchen and makes a big speech about how to cut the perfect slice. This year, while he was busy talking, the dog quietly hopped up onto the kitchen chair.
By the time Dad finished his speech, the dog had already helped itself to the first slice.

What's a pig's New Year's resolution?
To keep a cleaner pen.
What's a horse's New Year's resolution?
To keep stable habits.
What's an astronaut's New Year's resolution?
To make this year out of this world.
What's a photographer's New Year's resolution?
To focus on the good stuff.
What's a librarian's New Year's resolution?
To start a new chapter.
What's a tailor's New Year's resolution?
To mend a few old habits.
What's an electrician's New Year's resolution?
To stay current.
What's a weatherman's New Year's resolution?
To have a sunnier outlook.
What's a chef's New Year's resolution?
To spice things up this year.
Why is it so quiet on New Year's Day morning?
Everybody is sleeping in after midnight.
Why do people say 'See you next year!' on New Year's Eve?
It's the one night next year is only a few hours away.
Why did the boy say he hadn't brushed his teeth in a year?
He last brushed them at 11:59 on New Year's Eve.
What did Mom say at 12:01 on New Year's Day?
Last year's dishes are still in the sink.
Why did the snowflake come to the New Year's Eve party?
It wanted to start the year off cool.
Why is the New Year's Eve ball so shiny?
It polishes all year for one minute of fame.
Why does confetti love New Year's Eve?
It's the one night it gets thrown a party.
What did the broom say on New Year's Day?
Who brought all this confetti?
How long does New Year's Eve confetti last?
Till you find it in the couch next New Year's.
Why did the kitchen timer get invited to the New Year's Eve party?
Somebody had to keep the countdown honest.
What did the trash can say on New Year's Day?
Out with the old!
Why did the pencil get a new eraser on New Year's Day?
For all the times we'll write the wrong year.
Why did the new year bring a big backpack?
It had 365 days to carry.
What did the empty planner say on New Year's Day?
Please, somebody write something in me!
What's a church choir's New Year's resolution?
To hit every high note and get to practice on time.
Why did the church van make a New Year's resolution?
It wants to start on the first try every Sunday.
Why did the kids bang pots and pans on New Year's Eve?
Grandma said it was the only night that counts as music.
Why do hot chocolate sales go up on New Year's Eve?
Everybody's trying to stay warm and awake for midnight.
What do you call a New Year's resolution to read more?
A real page-turner of a plan.
What's the best thing about a brand-new year?
You get to try all your old resolutions again.
Why did the dog stay up till midnight on New Year's Eve?
It wanted to see if a new year meant new treats.
What do penguins say at midnight on New Year's Eve?
Ice to see you, new year!
Why did the kid write a list of New Year's resolutions for his little brother?
He figured those would be easier to keep.
Why did the boy put his New Year's resolutions in the freezer?
To keep them fresh till February.
What did December say on New Year's Eve?
It's been a great year, but I'm all out of days.
Why did Grandpa wear two watches on New Year's Eve?
He wasn't about to miss midnight this year.
What's the quietest moment of New Year's Eve?
The second right before everybody yells 'One!'

Grandpa promised the grandkids he would stay up till midnight on New Year's Eve. At ten-thirty he sat down in his recliner 'just to rest his eyes.' At 11:59 the kids gathered around his chair and started the countdown as loud as they could: 'Ten, nine, eight...' At 'one,' Grandpa popped open one eye.
'See? I told you I was just resting my eyes.' He was snoring again by 12:01.

A little girl asked her dad why people make New Year's resolutions. 'So we can try to be a little better this year,' he said. She thought it over and asked, 'Can I make one for you?' Dad laughed and said, 'Sure, sweetheart. What is it?'
'Share the TV remote.'

On New Year's Day, Mom said everyone in the family had to write down one resolution. Dad wrote 'exercise more.' Mom wrote 'read more books.' Big sister wrote 'be nicer to my little brother.' Little brother chewed on his pencil for a long time, then finally wrote his down.
It said, 'Help my sister keep her resolution.'

On January 2nd, Dad laced up his brand-new running shoes and announced he was going to jog every single day this year. Twenty minutes later he was back on the couch, red in the face and breathing hard. Mom asked how far he made it.
'Far enough to find out my New Year's resolution needs a resolution.'

As the New Year's Eve countdown got close, a little boy climbed up on the couch. 'Three, two, one!' At 'one,' he jumped as high as he could and landed on the cushions. His mom asked him what in the world he was doing.
'I wanted to say I jumped into the new year!'

On the first day back at school after New Year's, the teacher asked the class what they'd learned over the break. One boy raised his hand and said, 'I learned that a whole year can go by in one minute.' 'How's that?' the teacher asked.
'At 11:59 it was last year. One minute later, it wasn't!'

Grandma put black-eyed peas, collard greens and cornbread on the table for New Year's Day dinner. 'Eat up,' she said. 'The peas are for good luck and the greens are for a good year at work.' Her grandson looked at every dish on the table, one at a time.
'Grandma, which dish gets me out of chores?'

Dad bought the biggest calendar in the whole store right after New Year's. 'This year I'm going to write everything down so I don't forget a thing,' he said. On January 10th, Mom found the calendar, still in the bag, behind the front seat of the truck.
Dad said, 'So that's where I put it. I forgot.'

A little boy begged to stay up till midnight on New Year's Eve for the first time. At nine he was bouncing off the walls. At ten he was yawning. By eleven he was sound asleep on the couch. His parents woke him at midnight, and he mumbled 'Happy New Year' and fell right back asleep.
The next morning he told everyone at breakfast, 'I stayed up the whole night!'

A gym owner told his friend, 'Every January, thanks to New Year's resolutions, our place is so packed you have to wait in line for a treadmill. By February, it's empty. So this year I'm trying something new. I'm charging by the visit instead of by the month.'
His friend said, 'That's a great plan. You'll be broke by Groundhog Day.'

Grandpa set up the New Year's fireworks in the gravel driveway, with a bucket of water nearby and all the kids watching from the porch. He lit the first one. It fizzled. He lit the second one. It fizzled too. So did the third. 'Grandpa, what's wrong with them?' the kids asked.
'I've had these in the garage so long, I think they retired before I did.'

A family in Missouri wanted to ring in the new year with their cousins in California. At midnight, everybody in Missouri cheered, blew their noisemakers and called the cousins on speakerphone. 'Happy New Year!' they shouted. The cousins said, 'We've still got two more hours out here!'
Grandpa leaned toward the phone and said, 'Well, call us back and tell us how it ends.'

A man told his friend that his New Year's resolution was to stop putting things off. In March, the friend ran into him at the hardware store and asked how the resolution was going. The man smiled and nodded.
'Going great. I'm starting it tomorrow.'

A little girl asked Grandma why the family always eats black-eyed peas on New Year's Day. 'It's tradition,' Grandma said. 'My mama did it, and her mama did it before her.' The girl thought about it and asked, 'But who started it?'
Grandma said, 'Somebody who had a whole lot of black-eyed peas and needed a good reason to cook them.'

On New Year's morning, Mom packed all the leftover cookies into a box and said, 'My resolution starts today. No more sweets.' That afternoon she opened the box to give the cookies away, and every last one was gone. Everyone looked at Dad.
Dad said, 'I was just helping you keep your resolution.'

On the first week of school after New Year's, the teacher noticed a student had written last year at the top of his paper. 'You wrote last year's date,' she said. The boy sighed and put his pencil down.
'I know. I'm not ready to give it back yet. I never finished my homework from it.'

Grandpa insisted on leading the New Year's Eve countdown this year. Nobody had the heart to stop him when he started at one hundred, slow and careful, at 11:58. 'Fifty-two... fifty-one... fifty...' By the time he finally got down to one, the clock said 12:02.
Grandma patted his hand and said, 'Happy New Year. Two minutes late, just like every year.'

A boy handed his mom his list of New Year's resolutions. She read it out loud: 'Eat more candy. Stay up later. Skip vegetables. Get a puppy.' She looked at him and said, 'Honey, these aren't resolutions. This is a wish list.'
'I know, Mom. But these are the only ones I know I'll keep.'

A little boy watched the big ball drop on TV for the very first time on New Year's Eve. He stared with his mouth open as it slid down the pole and the whole crowd cheered. When it reached the very bottom, he gasped and grabbed his dad's arm.
'Uh oh, Daddy. Who's going to pick it back up?'

After New Year's, Mom hung the new calendar on the fridge and filled it with birthdays, dentist visits, church potlucks, ball games and school programs. When she finished, every single square was full. Dad studied it for a long time and asked where she'd written down a day to rest.
Mom said, 'February 30th.'
On New Year's Day, a little boy asked, 'Grandpa, what was your New Year's resolution when you were my age?' Grandpa said, 'To get taller.' The boy looked up at him. 'Did it work?' he asked.
'It took me about ten years, but yes, I kept that one.'

At the first church service of the new year, the pastor asked everyone who had made a New Year's resolution to stand up. Half the church stood. Then he asked everyone who had already broken theirs to sit back down. Everyone sat down except Mrs. Johnson.
'What was your resolution?' the pastor asked. She said, 'To stand up more in church.'

At New Year's Day dinner, Grandma told the kids to eat one black-eyed pea for every day they wanted good luck this year. Little Sam carefully counted out exactly five peas, ate them, and pushed the rest of the bowl away. 'Only five days?' Grandma asked.
'Yes ma'am. Monday through Friday. Saturdays and Sundays are already lucky.'

Uncle Ray's New Year's resolution was to be on time for everything. He was so proud of it that he told everybody about it the minute he walked in for New Year's Day dinner. Then he looked around and asked why everyone was already eating dessert.
Aunt Linda said, 'Ray, dinner was at noon. It's three o'clock.'

On New Year's Eve, a little boy asked his grandpa, 'What happens to the old year after midnight?' Grandpa leaned back and thought for a minute. 'Well, it goes into the photo albums, the stories and the memories,' he said. The boy nodded slowly.
'So that's why you tell the same stories every year. You're going back to visit.'

Mom's New Year's resolution list was three pages long: exercise, read more, clean out the garage, learn to sew, call the cousins more and drink more water. Dad's list had just one line on it. Mom read it and laughed out loud.
It said, 'Same as last year, since I never got around to it.'

On New Year's Day, a boy asked his grandma if she'd made any resolutions. 'At my age, honey, I only make one,' she said. 'I make the same one every year.' The boy asked what it was, and she said, 'To keep doing everything exactly the way I like it.'
'How's it going?' he asked. 'Perfect,' she said. 'I've never broken it once.'
